### Frameworks / formulas
- ARA objection framework — Acknowledge (show you heard them), Respond (tell them something they haven't considered), Ask (for permission to pitch, or for the meeting/demo) (Matt Macnamara — "3 Steps to CRUSH Cold Call Objections to Book More Meetings")
- Two objection buckets: brush-offs (hit in first 3-5 sec, objecting to the call not the offer) vs. real/business objections (budget, competitor, timing) — diagnose by *when* it lands (Matt Macnamara — "3 Steps to CRUSH Cold Call Objections to Book More Meetings")
- Feel-Felt-Found for incumbent objections: "A lot of our customers felt the same way — they felt they were all set… then when they evaluated us, what they found was [differentiator/result]." (Matt Macnamara — "3 Steps to CRUSH Cold Call Objections")
- Chet Holmes Buyer's Pyramid: ~3% buying now, ~7% open, ~30% not thinking about it, ~30% don't think they're interested, ~30% never will. The middle 60% is the influenceable market (Matt Macnamara — "3 Steps to CRUSH Cold Call Objections")
- Five Chris Voss "Never Split the Difference" objection techniques: selective word mirroring, labeling, mislabeling, accusation audits, ledge statements — plus calibrated questions (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Selective word mirror: repeat the last 1-3 critical words back as a question, inflecting up — "your price is too high" → "Too high?" — shows listening and elicits elaboration (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Labeling: open with "It sounds like… / It seems like… / It looks like…" to show you hear them and draw out more (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes" / "I Read 50 Sales Books")
- Mislabeling: deliberately label something *wrong* so the prospect corrects you — surfaces hidden objections (e.g. "it seems like this isn't a big enough problem to solve now") (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Accusation audit: pre-empt the negative — "You're probably going to think this is a ridiculous ask, but…" / "You probably think you could get XYZ cheaper elsewhere" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Ledge statements buy ~1 second and de-escalate: "That makes sense." / "That's exactly why I called." / "I expected you to say that." / "I'm with you." — avoid "I understand" (it's a tell) (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Isolate the objection (first objection is often a smoke screen): "[Objection] aside, is there anything else holding you folks back from moving forward?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- GAP Selling: map Current State → Future State; the difference is "the gap" — that's what they buy. Problem-centric, not seller-centric (Matt Macnamara — "Battle of the Sales Methodologies")
- "The problem defines the budget" (Keenan): a big enough problem self-justifies budget, authority, and timing — so you never have to interrogate for BANT (Matt Macnamara — "Battle of the Sales Methodologies")
- BANT = Budget, Authority, Need, Timing; MEDDIC = Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain, Champion — both seller-centric qualifiers (Matt Macnamara — "Battle of the Sales Methodologies")
- Cold email production system: (1) segment list by trigger (growth, funding, job postings, role), (2) build one personalized + one relevant template per problem you solve, (3) drop in research and send in 2-3 min (Matt Macnamara — "Write a Personalized Cold Email in 7 Minutes or LESS")
- Template build method: jot every problem your product solves in plain 5th-grade English, write the solution under each, then tie personalization into a problem via a transition (Matt Macnamara — "Write a Personalized Cold Email in 7 Minutes or LESS")
- Strong cold-call opener (Connect & Sell), verbatim: "Francois, thanks for taking my call. It's Matt with XYZ. Listen — I know my call is an interruption to your day. Can I have 27 seconds to tell you why I called?" 27 = a finite, oddly specific number that piques interest (Matt Macnamara — "2 Cold Call Opening Lines that Nail the First 15 Seconds")
- 4 ingredients of a strong cold-call opener: (1) permission-based, (2) shows assertiveness/control, (3) sincere, (4) you earn the right to analogy and pacing (Matt Macnamara — "2 Cold Call Opening Lines that Nail the First 15 Seconds")
- Discovery-call/demo agenda + "upfront contract," verbatim: confirm time/hard stops → "Here's what we're looking to accomplish… want your buy-in toward this game plan" → discovery-before-demo → name the two outcomes (interested = plan next step / not interested = tell me) → "This is your time — what would you add to that agenda?" (Matt Macnamara — "This is My Agenda that I Use to Kickoff Every Sales Discovery Call & Demo")
- The "upfront contract" — state the two acceptable end-states (next step or a clean no) at the START so you never leave without a decision; getting them to edit the agenda signals buy-in (Matt Macnamara — "This is My Agenda…" / "I Read 50 Sales Books" / "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script")
- Rapport in 1-2 min via research, not weather: "Francois, just saw you guys acquired Randori — curious, how's that going to impact your role?" (Matt Macnamara — "This is My Agenda that I Use to Kickoff Every Sales Discovery Call & Demo")
- Hormozi CLOSER framework: Clarify why they're there → Label them with the problem → Overview past pain ("I'm assuming I'm not the first you've dated…") → Sell the vacation (3-min pitch, problems not features) → Explain away concerns → Reinforce post-close to lift LTV / cut churn & refunds (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips" / "Alex Hormozi's C.L.O.S.E.R. Framework Explained By Sales Rep")
- "Selling is a transference of belief over a bridge of trust." Belief and trust are continuums — ask "how MUCH rapport did I build," not "did I build rapport" (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips")
- The "but"/"because" amplifier: everything after "but" is amplified, everything before diminished — own true negatives first to make the following positive more believable (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips")
- Ghost products / "sacrificial lambs": deliberately tell the prospect they can get item X cheaper elsewhere; acting against your own interest buys trust and lifts close rate on everything you DO recommend (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips")
- The assumed close: don't ask IF they want it, ask WHICH one ("Chocolate or vanilla?") — both options are a yes; strongest upsell in business (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips")
- "Only three things come out of your mouth on a sales call: questions, restatements ('it sounds like XYZ, am I hearing that right?'), and stories" — aim for 75-80% of talk in these three (Matt Macnamara — "Alex Hormozi's C.L.O.S.E.R. Framework Explained By Sales Rep")
- Pitch order: solve problems most-pain-to-least-pain; show the most powerful feature FIRST; "stories sell, features don't"; pitch ≤3 minutes, no jargon like "integration"/"implementation" (Matt Macnamara — "Alex Hormozi's C.L.O.S.E.R. Framework Explained By Sales Rep")
- Gary Vee "grab it" outbound: Google your niche, click businesses already paying to advertise there, find their number, cold call to pitch — go after advertisers who've proven they spend (Matt Macnamara — "Gary Vee Sales Tips for 18 Minutes Straight")
- Counterpuncher pitch model: prepare holistically (know your stuff cold), then reverse-engineer and deploy the client's needs in the moment — wing the delivery, not the content (Matt Macnamara — "Gary Vee Sales Tips for 18 Minutes Straight")
- "The second chess move first": play long-term — be willing to say "you don't need us, you need this" so the room recommends you for years (Matt Macnamara — "Gary Vee Sales Tips for 18 Minutes Straight")
- Daily reps ritual: each morning run objection-handling flashcards (objection on one side, scripted response on the other) + rehearse your top 7-10 pitches (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Day in the Life")
- 4-line "Obs" / "OPS" cold email: (1) Observation about the account, (2) Problem tied to it, (3) one-sentence solution statement, (4) soft interest-based CTA, plus a personalized PS; keep ≤150 words (Matt Macnamara — "The Cold Email Template that Outperforms ChatGPT EVERY Time" / "this has landed me 10+ offers in tech sales. STEAL IT")
- Cold email rules: avoid the word "I" (seller-focused), no emojis, no bullet points, sentences "super short and crispy" (Matt Macnamara — "The Cold Email Template that Outperforms ChatGPT EVERY Time")
- Cold call script (Ronan Pastor, 183 meetings/yr): Permission opener → "have you heard of us" qualifier → probing question (a current pain) → if "no," provocative future-oriented question tied to your solution → ask for the meeting; run in 1-2 min (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script that Books 1 Meeting/Day")
- Permission-based opener (verbatim): "Hey Chris, it's Matt with IBM — how have you been?" → "I know nobody likes getting a cold call, especially on a Friday afternoon right before a long weekend, so I can keep it super brief and then you can decide if you want to hang up — sound fair?" (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script that Books 1 Meeting/Day")
- Go-to permission opener (verbatim): "Chris, thanks for taking the call. Listen, you're probably going to hate me for this — this is actually a cold call. Do you want to hang up, or can I steal a minute to tell you why I called?" (~80% pass) (Matt Macnamara — "Cold Calling Advice from an ACTUAL Cold Caller" / "2 Cold Call Opening Lines")
- Tonality > words: open with "how have you been" not "how are you" — a 90,000-call Gong study found it the single best-performing opener; it scrambles the prospect's mind and buys seconds (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script that Books 1 Meeting/Day")
- "Humble disclaimer" before a probing question: "Out of curiosity Chris — and this isn't a gotcha — but do you have any way of knowing which customers are feeling the most frustrated this month?" (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script that Books 1 Meeting/Day")
- Provocative/future-oriented question after a "no": "That's actually why I was reaching out — have you considered using AI to track frustration/urgency from each support ticket, so you know where the fires are starting before they land on your desk?" (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script that Books 1 Meeting/Day")
- No-oriented meeting ask: "Would it be crazy if we found 30 minutes next week to explore in more detail?" then "How does Tuesday at 3pm work?" (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script that Books 1 Meeting/Day")
- Discovery/demo call structure (42% close rate): Agenda + upfront contract → Discovery → recap before demo → demo to their specific problem → transition to close → share price → uncover timeline + authority → book next step live (Matt Macnamara — "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script & Software Demo Guide")
- Upfront contract = TGAU: Time (hard stops?), Goal, Agenda, Upfront contract — agree the call ends one of two ways: schedule a next step, or a clean no (Matt Macnamara — "I Read 50 Sales Books" / "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script")
- "Discovery prompter" for outbound: a short narrative listing 3 problems people like them face, ending "I don't know how much of that sounds like your world, and what I missed that you're focused on?" (Matt Macnamara — "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script & Software Demo Guide")
- "Problem/priority drop" on a cold call: present three problems the prospect might face and see which is relevant — instead of a me-focused pitch (Matt Macnamara — "Cold Call Pro Reacts to a Beginner's First Cold Calls EVER")
- "Promise value without a pitch" (The Lost Art of Closing): "It sounds like there's a bit of interest — would you be opposed to connecting? Whether or not you do business with us, you'll likely ask different questions and make different decisions because of it." (Matt Macnamara — "I Read 50 Sales Books")
- Open with "The reason for the call is..." — people crave reasons, especially from a salesperson calling out of the blue (Matt Macnamara — "Cold Call Pro Reacts to a Beginner's First Cold Calls EVER")
- Permission-based opener (4-objection live call): "This is [name] with [company]. You're actually not expecting this call — first time I've tried to reach you. Mind if I share why I'm calling and you let me know if it's relevant or not?" (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Call that Booked a Meeting While Handling Four Objections!")
- Have-2-questions-ready rule: prep questions around 2+ value props so when the prospect deflects the first, you pivot to a backup and keep probing (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Call that Booked a Meeting While Handling Four Objections!")
- Arman Farooq cold-call script (booked 1 in 4): Step 1 "Have you heard our name tossed around?" → Step 2 "The reason I reached out…" triggering-problem proposition (specific problem in 5th-grade language + one-sentence solution + low-pressure ask) → Step 3 Mr. Miyagi objection method (Matt Macnamara — "This Cold Call Script I Just Learned is a Problem")
- Mr. Miyagi objection method: 1) agree with the objection, 2) split it (diagnose what's really behind it), 3) sell the meeting, not the product (Matt Macnamara — "This Cold Call Script I Just Learned is a Problem")
- Discovery kickoff "housekeeping" sequence: Rapport → Objective → Time check → Agenda → Upfront Contract; order flexible, must feel natural (Matt Macnamara — "This is How You Start a Sales Discovery Call with a Potential Client")
- Maps/Waze analogy: setting objective + agenda is like punching the address into Google Maps before you drive — gives the prospect a roadmap (Matt Macnamara — "This is How You Start a Sales Discovery Call with a Potential Client")
- Blank LinkedIn connection request converts best — no personalization. Connect, wait two days, then follow up with a personalized voice/video message (Matt Macnamara — "The Best LinkedIn Connection Request Message for Salespeople")
- NEPQ disarming reframe (Jeremy Miner): don't tell them why to buy — find out why they'd want to change and let them defend it: "I'm not quite sure you should yet… we'd have to understand more about X to see if we can even help — maybe you don't even need us." (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- NEPQ tonality + 3-second pause: soften into a "concern tone" showing empathy; deliver slowly with a 3-sec pause. Asking fast = surface answers; a defensive tone gets a defensive reaction (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- NEPQ "diffusing question": when you spot hesitation, address it before closing — "I noticed when I went over [X] you seemed a bit hesitant — what's behind that, just so I understand?" (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- NEPQ neutral language: swap assumptive words for neutral ones ("might," "possible," "if you feel this is what you're looking for") and end with "Would that help you?" (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- NEPQ "F-bomb" rule: never "I'm just following up" / "checking back in" (reads as "calling for your money") → re-language to "I just had time to get back to you" (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- NEPQ trigger-curiosity opener: sounding 100% confident flags you as a salesperson and triggers fight-or-flight; instead act slightly unsure ("um, this is Jeremy… wondering if you could possibly help me out for a moment?") (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- "Our other clients" not "ALL our other clients" — dropping "all" stays believable without implying some clients fail (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- Reverse-engineer the buyer before selling: spend dedicated time NOT selling, just listening, to map their real pain points first (Matt Macnamara — "Gary Vee Sales Tips for 18 Minutes Straight")

### VOC language
- Brush-off objections (verbatim): "Not interested." / "Is this a sales call?" / "Email me." / "I don't take cold calls." / "I'm running into a meeting." / "I'm busy." (Matt Macnamara — "3 Steps to CRUSH Cold Call Objections" / "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Real business objections (verbatim): "We already have a solution in place." / "We already have a vendor." / "Your competitor is cheaper." / "That's out of my budget." / "We only have X dollars." (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Stalling objections (verbatim): "I need to think about it." / "I'll get back to you." / "Send me an email." / "Call me back next quarter." / "I need to speak with my partner/wife/CFO." (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Incumbent brush-off (verbatim): "To get a meeting in our space you really have to have deep expertise — an outsourced version of that has never worked for us." (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Calling: The Prospect Laughed 3 Times")
- Dream-outcome / envy language: "they cleared north of $450,000 in W2 income last year," "made five President's Clubs," "driving a fancier car, a nicer house, a cooler life than me" (Matt Macnamara — "This is ruining my sales career")
- Buyer pain framing: prospects fear "off-target earnings"; reps worry they'll "land on the chopping block" in a layoff and that a PIP is "a death sentence" (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales MINUS the lies and deception")
- Prospect's internal monologue on a weak cold call: "I don't know a Matt, I don't know what XYZ company… who is this and what's this about?" (Matt Macnamara — "2 Cold Call Opening Lines that Nail the First 15 Seconds")
- Stall objections (verbatim): "No thank you" / "I need to think about it" / "I gotta talk to my spouse" / "not sure if it's a fit" / "I don't make fast decisions" / "I don't have the card on me" (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips")
- Spouse/authority objection (verbatim): "My husband's not going to approve that." (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips")
- Dream outcome in prospect's words: "I want to focus on growing the company without managing the ads all day long." (Matt Macnamara — "Iman Gadzhi's LIVE Sales Call EXPOSED")
- Distrust-of-agency VOC: "we added them as admin… one of their members got hacked, they hacked our whole business manager, removed all our ads, and didn't give the money back. It was a bad experience." (Matt Macnamara — "Iman Gadzhi's LIVE Sales Call EXPOSED")
- Price objection: "Thanks for meeting with us, but your price — it's just too high" (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Grant Cardone's 'Best' Sales Advice")
- Cheaper-competitor objection: "We met with XYZ and they're $50 and you're charging us $100" (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Grant Cardone's 'Best' Sales Advice")
- Budget objection (verbatim): "I just purchased this business at the beginning of the year, so I don't have a lot of money for marketing — but I'd love to hear what you've got" (Matt Macnamara — "Cold Call Pro Reacts to a Beginner's First Cold Calls EVER")
- No-urgency tell: "if it's not solved six months from now it'll be annoying, but we'll deal with it" vs. high urgency: "if this isn't solved six months from now, I'm probably not going to have a job" (Matt Macnamara — "Alex Hormozi's C.L.O.S.E.R. Framework Explained By Sales Rep")
- Blow-off objections usually BS: "I'm in a meeting," "I'm on a conference call," "I'm out to lunch with clients" (Matt Macnamara — "Cold Call Pro Reacts to a Beginner's First Cold Calls EVER")
- Gartner stat cited: 75% of prospects don't want to involve a salesperson to make a decision (up from 45% in 2021) (Matt Macnamara — "My Controversial Cold Call and Tech Sales HOT Takes")
- Brush-off (verbatim): "Possibly in the future, right now we're pretty happy with what we got and I don't have a lot of budget for any extra software at the moment." (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Call that Booked a Meeting While Handling Four Objections!")
- "I would love to, it sounds like you're up to great things, but look — I got no budget." (Matt Macnamara — "This Cold Call Script I Just Learned is a Problem")
- "We responded to the ad, but we're pretty happy with the company we use — I don't think we're interested." — knee-jerk get-rid-of-you reaction (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- Stalling objections (verbatim): "This sounds really good, but I need some time to think about it / I need to pray about it / I need to keep looking around." (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- "We already have a policy — why should we go with you?" (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- Insurance dream-outcome framing: "Who do you care most about… and if they pass away, do you have something set aside so they don't have to come out of pocket? Most people don't plan for death, they plan for everything else." (Matt Macnamara — "This guy might be WORSE than Grant Cardone & Andy Elliot")

### Offers / pricing / guarantees
- Risk-reversal phrasing for the ask: "to see if we might even be able to help" — frames the meeting as a mutual fit-check, not a pitch (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Calling: The Prospect Laughed 3 Times")
- "No strings attached" / "I don't want to strong-arm you into anything" — low-pressure framing that earns repeat asks on the same call (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Calling: The Prospect Laughed 3 Times")
- Reason-why for the ask: "the reason for my call was to see if it even makes sense for us to spend time together — and if it's not relevant, I won't reach back out again" (Matt Macnamara — "3 Steps to CRUSH Cold Call Objections")
- Value-justification close on price: get them to list every reason they'd pick you, then "So you could see why we're more." — they sell themselves on the premium (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Always share price on the first call — even a ballpark; withholding it pisses prospects off (Matt Macnamara — "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script & Software Demo Guide")
- Price-delivery word track (verbatim): "Chris, for your use cases, what you're looking at is $5 per device per month with a one-time setup fee of $1,500 — and I'm going to shut up" then go silent (Matt Macnamara — "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script & Software Demo Guide")
- "Reverse the rating" trust play (The Transparency Sale): people buy a 4.1-star product over a 5-star one; proactively share your flaws to disarm resistance (Matt Macnamara — "I Read 50 Sales Books")
- Risk-reversal cold-call opener: "I'll pitch you an idea, you give me 20 seconds, and if none of it applies you can hang up on me and I'll never call you back again. How does that sound?" (Matt Macnamara — "10 Live Cold Calls from 6 Different Sales Reps")
- Outcome-anchored ask: "I wanted to ask if I could show you a tool that could, at minimum, double the pipeline you generate — would you be willing to entertain a further discussion?" (Matt Macnamara — "10 Live Cold Calls from 6 Different Sales Reps")
- Discovery "refer you out" risk-reversal: "The goal today is to see if we can help. If we can, great. If we can't, no problem — I'll refer you out to another solution or competitor." (Matt Macnamara — "This is How You Start a Sales Discovery Call with a Potential Client")
- Clawback transparency close (anti-overselling): "It's not in my best interest to sell you something that isn't a fit — if it's not, my commission gets clawed back. So my intention is genuinely to help you." (Matt Macnamara — "This is How You Start a Sales Discovery Call with a Potential Client")
- SDR comp benchmark: median base $55K, OTE $80K at 100% of quota; below that, negotiate or walk (Matt Macnamara — "CRUSH Your FIRST SDR Interview to Break Into Tech Sales")

### Objection handling
- "Not interested" early (accusation audit): "You're probably going to think, Chris, I'm trying to sell you something you have no need for whatsoever." (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- "Not interested" after the pitch (ledge + calibrated question): "That makes sense. Before we hang up — is it because I called at the worst possible time, or are you happy with what you have?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- "I'm heading into a meeting / busy": "That makes sense — I'm calling completely out of the blue. Can I steal just 30 seconds to tell you why I called, and you can let me know if it's worth calling back?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- "We already have a vendor": label it ("Sounds like they're doing a great job"), let them talk, then accusation audit + no-question: "Would it be a ridiculous idea to explore opportunities beyond what you have today… so if your situation changes you have someone in your back pocket?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- "Call me back next quarter" / "Send me an email" (go for the no): "Typically when folks tell me to send an email, what they really mean is it's going straight in the trash — you won't hurt my feelings if that's the case. Am I off base?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- "Your price is too high" (isolate → label → reframe): "Price aside, is there anything else holding you back? … It sounds like the value just isn't here for you." (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- "Your competitor is cheaper": "If they're cheaper, why haven't you purchased XYZ already?" or "What motivated you to speak with me today?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- "I need to think about it": "It means one of two things — either you're not interested (you won't hurt my feelings) or you're interested but not 100% sure yet. Of those two, how do you feel?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- "I need to speak with my partner/CFO": don't try to close — isolate, then set a joint call: "Better to address those questions together. How difficult would that be to set up? What hesitations has he had in the past?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- "Is this a sales call?" (be brutally honest): "It actually is — but not the way you're thinking. The reason for my call was to see if the research I did on your company is right and my product might be able to help you [value]." (Matt Macnamara — "3 Steps to CRUSH Cold Call Objections")
- Brush-off reframe that converted live: "Large ASPs is exactly what we specialize in" (confident tone) → "that's actually why I was reaching out" (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Calling: The Prospect Laughed 3 Times")
- Principle: tonality, pacing, friendly tone, laughs matter far more than the words — it's what lets you ask 3 times on one call without being pushy (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Calling: The Prospect Laughed 3 Times")
- Childlike-curiosity reframe (never argue): meet every objection with "Huh, that's so interesting — why do you think that? Tell me more." (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips")
- Spouse objection via questions, not rebuttal: "Why wouldn't he? He wants what's best for you, right? Does he know you're struggling with this? Would he be happier if you kept struggling? Then would you be opposed to moving forward today?" (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips")
- "Expect and plan for the no — it's not failure, it's expected. If they were just going to buy, you wouldn't be needed." (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips")
- Never say "I'm going to be 100% honest with you" — it implies everything before was a lie (Matt Macnamara — "Iman Gadzhi's LIVE Sales Call EXPOSED")
- Don't present price/offer until the prospect verbally confirms you're a viable solution — "there's no point presenting price to somebody who doesn't believe you can solve the problem." (Matt Macnamara — "Iman Gadzhi's LIVE Sales Call EXPOSED")
- "If the price was the same" (Grant Cardone): "If the price was the same, who would you rather do business with — us or the cheaper solution?" → "us" → "Curious, why?" → exhaust every reason → "So you can see why we charge a bit more" then shut up (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Grant Cardone's 'Best' Sales Advice")
- Cheaper-competitor reframe: "Wow, they're charging $50? If I were you I'd go with them. Curious — why are you still talking to me?" (the reason they're still talking = your product is better) (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Grant Cardone's 'Best' Sales Advice")
- "I'm not interested" menu reframe: "I know it's not your job to help salespeople. Before hanging up — are you not interested because you're happy with what you have, you've got more pressing things, or you just hate cold calls as much as I hate making them?" (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Grant Cardone's 'Best' Sales Advice")
- "Out to lunch / in a meeting": "Gotcha — before hanging up, you mind if I steal 15 seconds to tell you why I called, and you let me know if it's worth calling back?" (Matt Macnamara — "Cold Call Pro Reacts to a Beginner's First Cold Calls EVER")
- No-budget reframe (go for value-give meeting): "Would you be opposed to learning a few strategies we've used to help other travel agencies convert more leads — some you can use today that don't cost a dime — so when your situation changes you've got someone in your back pocket?" (Matt Macnamara — "Cold Call Pro Reacts to a Beginner's First Cold Calls EVER")
- "Stay on the radar" passive ask: "I create a ton of content that might help you — would it be okay if from time to time I sent you a relevant email based on your business?" (Matt Macnamara — "Cold Call Pro Reacts to a Beginner's First Cold Calls EVER")
- Flaw-sharing reframe (verbatim): "I'm not sure if this is a showstopper, but that's not something we do a great job at. There are a few other products, ABC and XYZ, that do a much better job." then shut up (Matt Macnamara — "I Read 50 Sales Books")
- "Send me an email" — brush-off vs real: if early/no value discussed, name it: "Do you have something specific in mind for me to send, or no harm to ask, do you just want to get me off the phone?" (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Call that Booked a Meeting While Handling Four Objections!")
- "Send me an email" — when real, go for the meeting: "I've sent a lot of these and never had one person reply. Would it be totally crazy if we just set 20-30 minutes on the calendar?" (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Call that Booked a Meeting While Handling Four Objections!")
- "Bad time" handle (off permission opener): "Sounds like I might have caught you at a bad time — is it worth me sharing why I was calling to figure out if I should call back another time?" (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Call that Booked a Meeting While Handling Four Objections!")
- Unsure framing to lower resistance: "I'm not sure if this is of interest to you…" outperforms "Do you want a 30-min demo?" (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Call that Booked a Meeting While Handling Four Objections!")
- No-budget split + sell-the-meeting (Miyagi): "Keeping a tool is harder than asking for a new one. Is budget out for this cycle, or does asking mean ROI cases? Usually the people who get budget when it opens are the ones who know what's #1, 2, 3 on their list. So, open to a look — not for now, just so you know what's out there?" (Matt Macnamara — "This Cold Call Script I Just Learned is a Problem")
- Multi-ask low-pressure close: "This might never be a fit — but would it be a terrible idea to explore how we might help? If it becomes a priority, you've got someone in your back pocket. I promise you walk away with a few ideas that weren't on your radar." (Matt Macnamara — "This Cold Call Script I Just Learned is a Problem")
- "We're happy with our vendor" disarm (NEPQ): "That's not a problem — and I'm not sure we could even help yet. We'd have to understand more about what you're using and the results, because maybe you're better off staying. Are you opposed to a conversation around that, possibly?" (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- "Why should we go with you?" reframe: don't list "we're #1, best price, best service" — instead: "I'm not quite sure you should yet… maybe you don't even need us. Who do you have your policy with now?" (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- "What's causing you to want to replace them?" — ask so they defend the change themselves (self-persuasion is stronger) (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Jeremy Miner Sales Tips")
- "Mislabel" to open up a flat prospect: "It sounds like you have no need for any new clients" — provokes a correction (Matt Macnamara — "Cold Call Pro Reacts to a Beginner's First Cold Calls EVER")
- Interview-close (works for any sales conversation): "Based on our conversation, do you have any hesitations or concerns that would prevent you from moving me forward?" (Matt Macnamara — "Breaking into Tech Sales is HARD" / "CRUSH Your FIRST SDR Interview")

### Discovery questions
- Buying-process tease (better than "are you the decision maker?"): "Can you walk me through the steps you and your team need to take internally to make a definitive yes or no?" / "The last time you purchased technology like this, what did the process look like?" (Matt Macnamara — "Battle of the Sales Methodologies")
- Urgency tease (better than "what's your timeline?"): "If this proves to be the right solution, I want to match your urgency — when is the absolute latest you'd want this fully implemented?" (Matt Macnamara — "Battle of the Sales Methodologies" / "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script")
- GAP discovery — Current state: "Where are you today? What issues are you having and how is it affecting the business? What happens if you don't fix it?" Future state: "Where do you want to go? Why? How will you measure the outcomes?" (Matt Macnamara — "Battle of the Sales Methodologies")
- Price-comparison flip: "If my price were the same as ABC and XYZ, which solution would you rather use? Can you walk me through all the reasons why?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Budget probe (calibrated): "When you say you only have X dollars, does that mean only this quarter, or for the remainder of the year?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- Smoke-screen surfacer: "Objection aside, is there anything else holding you folks back from moving forward?" (Matt Macnamara — "EVERY sales objection handled in 30 minutes")
- "In 6 months' time, where would you need to be for you to consider this partnership a success?" (ask AFTER you've found the problem) (Matt Macnamara — "Iman Gadzhi's LIVE Sales Call EXPOSED")
- "It sounds like you're doing great and don't need our help — I'm curious, what motivated you to want to meet with us?" (surfaces the real reason fast) (Matt Macnamara — "Iman Gadzhi's LIVE Sales Call EXPOSED")
- "At the moment, what's stopping you from getting to that revenue number today?" (the problem-finding question) (Matt Macnamara — "Iman Gadzhi's LIVE Sales Call EXPOSED")
- Give-to-get: pair every question with the reason behind it, then follow up on the actual answer (active listening) (Matt Macnamara — "Iman Gadzhi's LIVE Sales Call EXPOSED")
- Replace dead-end questions ("Does that make sense?") with: "To what degree is this resonating so far?" / "To what extent do you find that useful?" / "How do you accomplish that today?" / "How does this compare to what you were expecting?" (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Day in the Life" / "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script")

- Pain-history question: "I'm assuming I'm not the first you've dated — is there anything you've tried in the past that got you here and didn't work?" (Matt Macnamara — "22 Minutes of the BEST Alex Hormozi Sales Tips")
- Gary Vee value-first discovery: "Let's cut the crap: what are your pain points, what are your struggles in your business?" (Matt Macnamara — "Gary Vee Sales Tips for 18 Minutes Straight")
- Clarify why they're there (outbound): "I bet you ignore 99% of outreach — what intrigued you about that cold email, and why did you take the time today?" (Matt Macnamara — "Alex Hormozi's C.L.O.S.E.R. Framework Explained By Sales Rep")
- The win question: "What's the one thing you want to accomplish on today's call, so we make sure it's productive?" (Matt Macnamara — "Alex Hormozi's C.L.O.S.E.R. Framework Explained By Sales Rep")
- Label-the-problem combo: "It sounds like you're up against X, it's impacting Y, the implications are Z — am I hearing that correctly or am I off base?" (Matt Macnamara — "Alex Hormozi's C.L.O.S.E.R. Framework Explained By Sales Rep")
- The "magic moment" question: "That problem sounds like it sucks — when was the moment you guys realized that was a problem?" (gets them to relive peak pain) (Matt Macnamara — "Alex Hormozi's C.L.O.S.E.R. Framework Explained By Sales Rep")
- Overview past pain: "I have to assume you tried to solve this — can you walk me through what you've tried? How did it work out? And outside of that, what else?" (exhaust it) (Matt Macnamara — "Alex Hormozi's C.L.O.S.E.R. Framework Explained By Sales Rep")
- Urgency qualifier: "What happens if the problem isn't solved six months from now?" — zero urgency means you won't close (Matt Macnamara — "Alex Hormozi's C.L.O.S.E.R. Framework Explained By Sales Rep")
- Get longer answers by starting questions with "help me understand…", "walk me through…", "tell me more about…" (Matt Macnamara — "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script & Software Demo Guide")
- Inbound discovery opener: "Can you walk me through what you're looking to accomplish by looking into XYZ solution?" (Matt Macnamara — "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script & Software Demo Guide")
- Transition-to-close: "What else were you hoping to see today that I brushed over?" → "Before we talk pricing — do you think this is a viable option to solve XYZ?" → "What excited you most about what you saw today?" (Matt Macnamara — "THE ULTIMATE Discovery Script & Software Demo Guide")

_All from Matt Macnamara (Sales niche). Several were pure career-vlog/mindset content (e.g. "Reminder it's all going to work out", "Sales & Depression", "Tech Sales EXPOSED", "SDR money", role-comparison) with nothing copy-relevant — processed, not extracted._

### Hooks / headlines / subject lines
- Cold email subject lines should be all-lowercase, 1-2 words, emotional + vague: "this sucks", "awful", "headache", "really cool", "hate this", "annoying" — vagueness drives the open ("they're thinking *what* sucks") (Matt Macnamara — "The GOAT Cold Email Strategy")
- The "triplet" subject line = expected + expected + UNexpected, e.g. "iPhones, Verizon, my girlfriend" — odd third element builds curiosity; first line ties all three (claims 60% open rate, credits Josh Braun) (Matt Macnamara — "The GOAT Cold Email Strategy")
- Ghosted/no-show re-engagement: subject "did i lose you" (lowercase), empty body, replied to the original invite — his highest reply-rate email (Matt Macnamara — "pov 30 year old guy surviving tech sales")
- Avoid questions/question marks in subject lines — claims they cut opens ~56% (reads like marketing, demands effort) (Matt Macnamara — "The GOAT Cold Email Strategy")
- Cold email opening lines should never start with "I" — buyer-focused openers: "noticed on your…", "saw on your website…", "looking at your LinkedIn…", "your peers have been…" (Matt Macnamara — "The GOAT Cold Email Strategy")
- Pattern-interrupt opener: "Hi [first name], JK I know your name is Chris. Are you open to a different perspective for [goal] without [annoying problem]? No? You don't have to [annoying problem]." (Matt Macnamara — "The GOAT Cold Email Strategy")
- Best video-email subject line: "this sucks [video]" — self-deprecating + the word "video" lifts opens (Matt Macnamara — "Hate Cold Calling? Do these 4 Things Instead to Book 1 Meeting/Day")
- "8 cold email first sentences that motivate a prospect to open your cold email and read the second sentence." (Matt Macnamara — "8 Cold Email First Sentences that Motivate Prospects to Click Open")
- Put the mutual connection's name IN the subject line when name-dropping a shared contact — lifts opens (Matt Macnamara — "8 Cold Email First Sentences that Motivate Prospects to Click Open")
- Avoid entirely: "Dear [Name], I hope all is well" / "I hope you're doing well in these trying times" — "99% of cold emails start the same way." (Matt Macnamara — "8 Cold Email First Sentences that Motivate Prospects to Click Open")
- "250 — that's the number of working days in 2025. My goal: book on average one meeting per day through cold calls." (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script to Book 250 Meetings in 365 Days")
- "This might be you right now — you feel like you're standing on a street corner begging for an interview, a chance to break into tech sales." (Matt Macnamara — "If I Had to Break Into Tech Sales, this is What I Would Do")
- Elevator-pitch open with a vivid problem-story, not "hi my name is": "You ever see those news stories where a company gets hit with a cyber attack — a hacker steals the data, holds it ransom, the company gets dragged through the mud and loses customer trust? Well, that's what I do." (Matt Macnamara — "4 Steps to Build Your Elevator Pitch in 3 Minutes")
- "Seven former co-workers quit tech sales in the last 12 months — burned out, laid off, done. But I'm still here and I'm not going anywhere." — concrete-number contrarian opener (Matt Macnamara — "Everyone is Leaving Tech Sales. Here's Why I'm Not.")
- Specific-number result hook: "This Crazy Sales Prospecting Technique Booked Me 17 Meetings… a 40% conversion rate to a meeting." (Matt Macnamara — "This Crazy Sales Prospecting Technique Booked Me 17 Meetings")
- Raw-vulnerability / anti-guru hook: "I'm at 6% to my sales quota… out of eight account executives I'm in last place by a far margin." (Matt Macnamara — "I'm at 6% to my sales quota")
- Authority-by-volume: "After Reading 40 Books on Sales — Here's What Works in 2025" (distills 40 down to ~10) (Matt Macnamara — "After Reading 40 Books on Sales")
- Name-the-competition pattern-interrupt: "You just landed an SDR interview… guess what, 15 other candidates did too. Everyone says the same things — but nobody except you will do this." (Matt Macnamara — "Try This SDR Sales Interview HACK")
- Bold superlative framing for a teardown: "best live cold call on the internet and it's not even close." (Matt Macnamara — "Reacting to the UK's Most Hated Sales Trainer's VIRAL Cold Call")
- Aspirational swipe-the-pro angle: "Be Better Than The Wolf" — teardown of a famous script as a content/positioning hook (Matt Macnamara — "Watch Me Breakdown & Improve the Original Stratton Oakmont Sales Script")
- Be the "1 out of 10," not the "9 out of 10" — deliberately do the opposite of what every other seller does, in openers and everywhere (Matt Macnamara — "Watch Me Breakdown & Improve the Original Stratton Oakmont Sales Script")

### Frameworks / formulas
- **Permission-based / self-outing cold-call opener** (recurs across many videos, ~80% earn the 30 sec): "[Name], it's [Name] with [Company]. You're probably going to hate me for this — this is actually a cold call. Want to hang up, or can I steal 30 seconds to tell you why I called? If you don't want to talk at the end, we end it there. Sound fair?" — delivered chill/friendly as a tonal pattern-interrupt (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script to Book 250 Meetings in 365 Days" / "Reacting to the UK's Most Hated Sales Trainer's VIRAL Cold Call" / "Live Cold Call that Booked the Appointment")
- **Disarming stranger opener** (Andre Kimman): "I'm an absolute stranger so don't rack your brain — I don't know you, you don't know me. Are you able to talk for a brief moment?" (Matt Macnamara — "Reacting to the GREATEST Cold Call ever made")
- **"Menu of pain" / discovery prompter / raising-problem-statement** (Benjamin Dennehy; "discovery prompter" is Gong's term): after permission, name 3 crispy, fifth-grade-level problems your buyers face, then "I get the feeling you're probably going to tell me none of this applies and I'm barking up the wrong tree." ~90% of the time one hits; if none land, they correct you and surface the real one (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script to Book 250 Meetings…" / "My EXACT Discovery Call & Demo Script" / "5 Step Discovery Call Script that Made Me $258K")
- **Sourcing the "crispy problems":** scrape job ads (Indeed/Glassdoor/LinkedIn) for the title you call — priorities/pains live in the listing — and interview your best customers about their day-to-day (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script to Book 250 Meetings…")
- **Competitor-priorities opener variant:** "In our work with [competitor] and [competitor], their [function] leaders focused on two priorities: [1], [2]. How does that compare to your focus at [their company]?" — competitors named must be well-known + similar (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script to Book 250 Meetings…")
- **Re-ask permission mid-call:** "I've had my 30 seconds — mind if we talk for one more minute?" — builds trust (Matt Macnamara — "Reacting to the UK's Most Hated Sales Trainer's VIRAL Cold Call")
- **Interest-based CTA over specific CTA:** "Does this sound like something worth exploring?" not "Can you meet Tuesday at 3?" — "time is finite, interest is not." (Matt Macnamara — "Reacting to the UK's Most Hated Sales Trainer's VIRAL Cold Call")
- **8 cold-email first-sentence templates** (Josh Braun): 1) "Unlike being X, [prospect] can't do Y" (relief); 2) The Wizard — "You must be a [skill] wizard, only way you survive [hard task]"; 3) "Are you open to X [benefit] without the headache of Y?"; 4) Common connection — "I stumbled across your name through our work with [named client]"; 5) Increased headcount — "I noticed you're hiring [role] in [city], suggests you're scaling [function]"; 6) name the specific admin grind they hate; 7) The Validator — genuine praise tied to the problem you solve; 8) Observation + question (Matt Macnamara — "8 Cold Email First Sentences…")
- **OPPPS / GOAT cold-email framework** (Brian LaManna): Observation (1-2 lines, buyer-focused) → Problem (must tie to the observation) → Solution ("[dept leaders] use [product] to [benefit]") → interest-based CTA → PS. (Earlier-batch shorthand "OPS" = same observation→problem→solution→CTA core.) (Matt Macnamara — "The GOAT Cold Email Strategy" / "Try This SDR Sales Interview HACK")
- **The PS is "the most-read part of any cold email"** yet reps skip it; uses: (1) point to another channel ("PS sent a LinkedIn connect if you prefer to chat there"), (2) offer alt CTA ("PS I could send a short vid"), (3) offer an out ("if this isn't relevant, let me know and I'll stop emailing") (Matt Macnamara — "The GOAT Cold Email Strategy")
- **7-step discovery system:** pre-call "get-intel" email + "set-the-stage" agenda email 24h prior (lifts show rates) → first 3 min set agenda (time check → goal → how → upfront contract → "what's the one thing you want to accomplish today?") → inbound-vs-outbound first question → questions that sell → transition to pitch (≤3 min) → book next step → recap email (Matt Macnamara — "My EXACT Discovery Call Script to Close (nearly) ANYONE 2025")
- **5-step discovery script** (Charles Muckbower): 1) intro + time-check ("I have us for 60 min, how are you on time? Any hard stops?"), 2) purpose + agenda + upfront contract, 3) find problem fast via menu of pain, 4) top questions / peel the onion, 5) pitch + close on next step (Matt Macnamara — "5 Step Discovery Call Script that Made Me $258K")
- **First-90-seconds, 3-element open:** align on Objective (destination) + Agenda (directions) + Next Decision (close-or-part-ways): "By the end I'd like to put you in a position to decide — schedule a next step, or we part ways as friends. Sound fair?" (Matt Macnamara — "My EXACT Discovery Call & Demo Script")
- **Upfront contract / "Rules of Engagement":** talk about the END of the call at the very start; soften with autonomy — "do you mind if we talk agenda? Here's what I'm thinking, let me know if you have a different one in mind… does that feel fair?" Controls the call while the buyer feels in control ("once you lose control of the car it's hard to get it back") (Matt Macnamara — "5 Step Discovery Call Script…" / "Genius SALES Advice that Works")
- **Inbound vs outbound first question:** Inbound → "Curious, what motivated you to look into [solution]?"; if they answer only in features, redirect → "what was the original *challenge* in your business that prioritized this?" Outbound → earn the right with the menu of pain first (Matt Macnamara — "My EXACT Discovery Call Script…2025")
- **Discovery "questions that sell" buckets:** find a problem ("What problems with your current [category] would you regret not solving 6 months from now?") → understand it ("Tell me more"; "I imagine you had a meeting about this — what did it sound like?"; "When did you realize it was a problem?") → what have they tried → focus on the right problem → impact ("How widely known is that pain in your org?") (Matt Macnamara — "My EXACT Discovery Call Script…2025")
- **GAP-selling / peel-the-onion:** treat the first answer as surface-level; ask 2-4 follow-ups per problem to uncover impact, who it affects, and business outcomes before moving on (Matt Macnamara — "After Reading 40 Books on Sales")
- **Question phrasing that pulls long answers:** lead with "walk me through…", "out of curiosity…", "talk to me about…", "help me understand…" instead of "how do you…" (Matt Macnamara — "My EXACT Discovery Call & Demo Script")
- **PIFF demo framework** — Pain → Impact → Feature → Feedback. State the prospect's pain + quantified impact BEFORE showing a feature; the setup matters more than the feature; end every feature with a micro-close/feedback question (Matt Macnamara — "My EXACT Discovery Call & Demo Script")
- **Five Commandments of demoing:** show the most important feature first (no ramp-up); solve pain 1-to-1; avoid "we can also" (overwhelms); orient them to the screen ("what you're looking at here is…"); micro-close throughout, not just at the end (Matt Macnamara — "My EXACT Discovery Call & Demo Script")
- **4-step close-out sequence:** 1) "Of the challenges we discussed, any I haven't addressed?" 2) verify viable option (get them to verbalize it) 3) buying process + "When's the absolute latest you'd want this implemented?" 4) "Mind if I recommend a next step?" then make a strong rec (Matt Macnamara — "My EXACT Discovery Call & Demo Script")
- **"Probe and provoke":** probe current-day pain ("do you already have a way to…") then provoke future possibility tied to your benefit ("have you considered tech that would… save you tons of time and stop deals from being lost?") (Matt Macnamara — "Reacting to the GREATEST Cold Call ever made")
- **Problem stack** (response to "I'm all set"): acknowledge + give kudos ("you're ahead of the curve"), then pivot to a 2nd/3rd differentiator via a probe: "When it comes to [next challenge], do you already have a way to prevent [issue]?" — requires knowing the deeper pains in advance (Matt Macnamara — "The BEST Cold Call Objection Handling Training" / "Reacting to the GREATEST Cold Call ever made")
- **Cold-call diagnostic funnel = AIDA on calls** (Attention→Interest→Desire→Action); track where prospects drop. Benchmark: 70-80% of "hello"s into permission-to-pitch; losing them here = opener sounds salesy (Matt Macnamara — "Reacting to the GREATEST Cold Call ever made")
- **4-step elevator pitch:** 1) open with an unexpected question, 2) "I *partner with*…" (stronger than "I help"), 3) take-pressure-off transition ("I'm not a fit for everyone, but if you have X we might"), 4) clear CTA (Matt Macnamara — "4 Steps to Build Your Elevator Pitch in 3 Minutes")
- **Three "Never Split the Difference" tactics:** Mirroring (repeat last 1-3 words with up-inflection — pulls info + buys thinking time); Labeling ("it sounds like…", "it seems like…"; labeling a negative defuses it); Go-for-No (no-oriented questions feel safer than yes) (Matt Macnamara — "Never Split the Difference 3 SALES Tips")
- **Mislabeling** (deliberate wrong label, used sparingly) to flush out truth: "it seems like you're still shopping around" / "doesn't seem like you're ready" — people love correcting salespeople (a "proof of life" check on whether you're the favorite) (Matt Macnamara — "Never Split the Difference 3 SALES Tips")
- **ARM objection framework:** Acknowledge (make them feel heard) → Respond (address it) → Meeting/Ask (no-oriented close) (Matt Macnamara — "The BEST Cold Call Objection Handling Training")
- **AIA objection framework:** Acknowledge → Isolate → Answer-and-ask ("Totally understand. Outside of [objection], any other reason you wouldn't move forward? … If I could show you X, would you consider Y?") (Matt Macnamara — "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice")
- **Knowledge-gap move:** ask a question BEFORE rebutting to expose what the prospect doesn't know ("Did the other contractor explain HOW they'd eat your deductible?" → "No" → now receptive). "Forget the word rebuttal — a rebuttal is a punch and kills trust." (Matt Macnamara — "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice")
- **Frontload objections in discovery:** list every objection you regularly get and deliberately raise each during discovery so it can't ambush you at the close ("objection whack-a-mole" is the amateur trap) (Matt Macnamara — "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice")
- **Ledge statement** (Jeb Blount, *Objections*): a memorized neutral auto-response ("That makes sense") that buys your brain 1-3 sec before you respond (Matt Macnamara — "After Reading 40 Books on Sales")
- **Three F's** (Sirois): Follow up (stay top of mind), Follow through (do what you said, when you said), Follow back (re-engage past customers — birthday, work anniversary, vacation note) (Matt Macnamara — "After Reading 40 Books on Sales")
- **30-day rule** (Jeb Blount): prospecting in this 30-day span pays off ~90 days out — "don't piss your future self off, prospect every day." (Matt Macnamara — "After Reading 40 Books on Sales")
- **Finite-focused-written-workable list** (Weinberg): a small deliberately-chosen account list resembling your best customers — same size, location, vertical, and crucially the same problems you solve (Matt Macnamara — "After Reading 40 Books on Sales")
- **Cold-call question rule:** use CLOSE-ended (yes/no) questions on cold calls to steer; save open-ended for discovery/demo — open-ended is too tall an ask of a stranger you just interrupted (Matt Macnamara — "STOP Asking These Types of Questions on Your Cold Calls")
- **Plain-English test:** if your grandma or a fifth-grader can't understand the problem statement, it won't hit — no jargon/buzzwords, keep it "crispy" (Matt Macnamara — multiple, incl. "5 Step Discovery Call Script…" / "Want an SDR role in Tech Sales? Do this…")
- **Video prospecting best practices:** subject includes "video"; animated GIF thumbnail; ≤45 sec; structure = company observation → tie to a problem → short solution → interest-based CTA; leave small mistakes in (feels authentic, lifts replies) (Matt Macnamara — "Hate Cold Calling? Do these 4 Things Instead…")
- **4 neglected prospecting channels:** handwritten notes, video prospecting, creative/dimensional outreach for A-accounts, and the closed-lost list (Matt Macnamara — "Hate Cold Calling? Do these 4 Things Instead…")
- **Creative/dimensional outreach (A-accounts only):** after calls/emails/DMs fail, send a personalized physical gift tied to a known interest (custom cupcakes; a missing Star Wars Pez to a collector; a custom Irish family-crest flag), then follow with a call — reserved for top accounts (Matt Macnamara — "This Crazy Sales Prospecting Technique Booked Me 17 Meetings")
- **A/B/C account tiering by spend:** A = personalized 1:1 off detailed CRM notes; B/C = short mass-blast email — segment so you don't burn months personalizing everything (Matt Macnamara — "Navigating Tech Sales: Day in the Life of Account Executive")
- **AI prep workflow:** in ChatGPT/Perplexity — "I'm meeting [name], tell me about him and his business; what interesting questions get at the impact of the problem; summarize as a one-pager." Cuts 2-hr prep to 10 min (Matt Macnamara — "Navigating Tech Sales: Day in the Life…")
- **Daily pre-call objection rehearsal:** run likely objections on index cards each morning — "never practice on your prospects." (Matt Macnamara — "Surviving Tech Sales: Day in the Life…")
- **"Sell me this pen" reframe** (Belfort): the rational move is to ask questions ("how long have you been in the market for a pen? what type? business or personal? how much do you spend?") — find the need first, weed out non-buyers (Matt Macnamara — "Genius SALES Advice that Works")
- **Interview "why this company" two-step:** 1) state your criteria for an ideal employer, 2) prove with specific research they meet it (tenure data, G2 counts, 10-K scan, ex-employee convos) (Matt Macnamara — "Mock Tech Sales Interview with Unemployed AE")
- **Job-search prospecting play:** filter target companies (≥60% SDR quota attainment, PMF ≥4/5), pick a top 10, find Directors/VPs of Sales Dev on Sales Nav, send blank connect → personalized video DM → email → apply; exhaust all 3 outcomes before expanding (Matt Macnamara — "If I Had to Break Into Tech Sales…")

### VOC language
- "I'm all set" / "we just switched vendors" / "thanks but we already use someone for that" — most common cold-call brush-offs (Matt Macnamara — "My girlfriend tries to stump me with cold calling objections")
- "Can you just send me an email?" — real meaning: "I'm going to hit delete… I'm not interested but don't want to hurt your feelings." (Matt Macnamara — "My girlfriend tries to stump me with cold calling objections")
- "Call me back next quarter" — soft no: "they want me to lose their number." (Matt Macnamara — "My girlfriend tries to stump me…")
- "I need to think about it" — usually one of two: (1) not interested but won't say, or (2) interested but unsure. (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Andy Elliot")
- The trust-killer: every seller claims "we have the best service, best pricing, best coverage" — prospects have heard it from every vacuum/car/insurance rep, so it commoditizes you and lowers trust (Matt Macnamara — "Genius SALES Advice that Works")
- Rep-in-distress / identity VOC: "I haven't gotten momentum in five months… spinning my wheels… tried anything and everything and nothing's working", "everybody else is killing it and you think you're the only one." (Matt Macnamara — "Unlike MOST Salespeople, I'm STRUGGLING")
- New-rep panic objections to train against: "no thank you", "I need to think about it", "I'm not sure", "I gotta talk to my spouse", "not sure it's a fit", "I don't make fast decisions", "I don't have the card I want to use on me." (Matt Macnamara — "Genius SALES Advice that Works")
- Brush-offs verbatim: "I'm running into a meeting"; "How'd you get this number? Is this a cold call? Take me off your list"; "I'm so busy, can you just email me?"; "Not interested"; "Don't call me back, I'll call you"; "I've never heard of you"; "I looked up your reviews and they don't look great"; "We don't have the budget"; "You clearly don't understand my business." (Matt Macnamara — "The BEST Cold Call Objection Handling Training" / "LIVE Role Playing Sales Objections" / "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice")
- The classic real competitive objection: "Oh, we're all set — we already got something for that." / "We're all good there." (Matt Macnamara — "The BEST Cold Call Objection Handling Training")
- Soft-no that means "I don't know" (worse than a no): "I'm curious to learn more… it's just not a burning priority." (Matt Macnamara — "Live Cold Call that Booked the Appointment")
- Buyer's-time grievance: "If you'll ask for my most valuable asset — my time — and won't spend 5 minutes on my website to prep, you don't deserve the rest of my time." (Matt Macnamara — "Navigating Tech Sales: Day in the Life…")
- Buyer fatigue: "About 80% of buyers don't want a salesperson involved — they'd rather talk to customer success and engineers." (Matt Macnamara — "Navigating Tech Sales: Day in the Life…")

### Offers / pricing / guarantees

- **Risk-reversal via payment-plan isolation:** "Is the money too much, or is it all-at-once — a cash-flow thing? If we broke it into three payments of $29.95, would that work? …then we're done." Isolate price vs timing, then reverse it (Matt Macnamara — "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice")
- **Cost-of-inaction reframe:** "Is it more expensive to prioritize this now and get to $10M/month, or more expensive to keep pushing it down the road and stay stuck at $5M?" (Matt Macnamara — "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice")
- **ROI claims reduce close rate ~27% if introduced before the prospect is sold** (cites Gong); ROI only works once they're sold and it justifies the decision — bury it inside a before/after customer story, don't lead with it (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Andy Elliot")
- **"If you didn't get a gasp from the price tag, you didn't go high enough"** — anchoring/pricing-courage principle for offer construction (Matt Macnamara — "Genius SALES Advice that Works")
- **Proof-of-concept / free trial as risk-reversal:** prospects who won't buy now get a 30-day POC to "test drive"; POCs convert at a stated ~70% close rate (Matt Macnamara — "Surviving Tech Sales: Day in the Life…" / "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Andy Elliot")
- **De-risk-the-decision proof offer (job interview):** "I have 10 prospects fitting your ICP I'll cold call — you vs. me, phone on speaker, right now. Want to give me feedback to improve my pitch?" Prove you can do the job before you're hired (Matt Macnamara — "The ELITE SDR Interview System")
- **Bold flat guarantee on a lead magnet:** "I guarantee you'll land that SDR job offer… nobody else is doing this, I promise, if you do this you WILL land the job" — tied to a free downloadable SDR sales-plan template (Matt Macnamara — "Try This SDR Sales Interview HACK")
- **Stalled-deal timeline qualifier:** "Is this a big enough problem to solve now rather than 6 months out?" If not a top priority, tentatively schedule ~5 months out instead of running a full eval (Matt Macnamara — "5 Step Discovery Call Script…")
- **Closing language (replace weak asks):** never "Are you ready to move forward?" → "Sounds like a perfect fit. Where do you want me to send the invoice — paying with credit, debit, or cash?" Ask with conviction (Matt Macnamara — "Sales in Movies: Cold Calling Breakdown from Boiler Room")

### Objection handling
- **"Send me an email"** → "Happy to — what do you want to see in it?" Specifics = real interest; "just general info" = no interest, go for the no. Or: "Typically when I email after a cold call I never hear back — it ends up in spam. Is this really something you want to look into, or just trying to get off the call? No worries either way." (Matt Macnamara — "My girlfriend tries to stump me…" / "Live Cold Call that Booked the Appointment")
- **"Take me off the list"** → disarm + reset: "Happy to. Sounds like you heard me and thought 'ugh, not another sales guy.' Can I have a chance to reset and level-set with you?" (Matt Macnamara — "The BEST Cold Call Objection Handling Training")
- **"How'd you get this number?"** → radical transparency: name the tool ("I use ZoomInfo — public company, gets data from all over the web"), then "I called to share how I might help, but I don't want to assume it's relevant — mind if I share for 30 sec, then you decide?" - **"I'm in a meeting"** → "That's on me, I caught you out of the blue. Mind if I share why I'm calling in 30 sec?" Be genuinely ready to walk if it's legit (Matt Macnamara — "The BEST Cold Call Objection Handling Training")
- **"Not interested" (early)** → "I think I'm reading the room — sounds like I sounded like the grimiest salesperson. Can I have a second chance? Do you believe in second chances?" - **"Maybe in 3-4 months"** → value-for-time exchange + no-oriented ask: "Would it be a terrible idea to find 30 min where I show how you *could* get this benefit — not even do it, just understand it — so when you're ready you know how it works?" (Matt Macnamara — "The BEST Cold Call Objection Handling Training" / "My girlfriend tries to stump me…")
- **"We just switched vendors"** → humor ("darn, just missed you!") + "Would it be a terrible idea to reconnect around renewal to explore options that might not be on your radar?" + ask to send relevant content to stay top of mind (Matt Macnamara — "My girlfriend tries to stump me…")
- **"We already use someone"** → "Awesome, sounds like they're doing great. Would it be a terrible idea to explore beyond what you have today — so you've got someone in your back pocket if you're ever in the market?" (Matt Macnamara — "My girlfriend tries to stump me…")
- **"We use [competitor]"** → never bash the competitor (their spouse may work there — true story); acknowledge, then move to your differentiator or problem-stack (Matt Macnamara — "The BEST Cold Call Objection Handling Training")
- **"I've never heard of you"** → "That's exactly why I'm calling — I didn't expect you to. Mind if I steal 60 sec to explain what we do and see if it's a fit?" (Matt Macnamara — "LIVE Role Playing Sales Objections")
- **"Bad reviews / why you?"** → "Honestly, I don't know if you should — I don't know enough about your situation. Mind if I ask a couple questions to see if you're even a fit? Happy to address those concerns too." (Matt Macnamara — "LIVE Role Playing Sales Objections")
- **"What makes you different?"** → "Good question — but I don't know if it even matters to you yet. Mind if I ask a few questions first, then I'll explain the differences?" (Matt Macnamara — "LIVE Role Playing Sales Objections")
- **"We don't have the budget"** → isolate first ("Outside of budget, anything else holding you back?"), then qualify timeframe to expose whether budget is a smokescreen for "we don't see the value." (Matt Macnamara — "LIVE Role Playing Sales Objections")
- **"I need to talk to my partner/spouse/CFO"** → isolate ("Outside of speaking with them, anything else?") → "What objections do you think they'd have?" / "If they said no, would you do it anyway?" → book a meeting with all decision-makers present (Matt Macnamara — "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice" / "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Andy Elliot")
- **"I'm too busy / not a good time"** → never disagree; "You want this to last long term, right? And you'll be busy again in the future too — so isn't it best to learn this while you're busy, so you can do it forever?" (Matt Macnamara — "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice")
- **"I need to think about it"** → label with a down-tone ("sounds like you have some hesitations") to draw out the real concern; or the two-options reframe: "Usually that means one of two things — not interested but don't want to tell me, or interested but not quite sure. Which fits?" (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Andy Elliot")
- **"I need to shop around"** → don't try to stop them: "When you think about this project, what's important to you? What's on your decision criteria?" Present fit honestly, even name competitors, then book a POC — "there's nothing you can do to stop somebody shopping; they should shop." (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Andy Elliot")
- **Hypothetical-isolation close:** "In a hypothetical world where [obstacle] didn't exist, would you say yes?" If yes, you now have one variable to solve (Matt Macnamara — "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice")
- **No-oriented question** (Camp/Voss): ask for the no — it feels safer than yes: "Would it be a ridiculous idea to explore this when I'm not cold-calling you out of the blue?"; "Is now a bad time?"; "Would you be opposed to connecting?"; ghosting email "Have you given up on this project?" instead of "Still interested?" (Matt Macnamara — "A Cold Call Script to Book 250 Meetings…" / "Never Split the Difference 3 SALES Tips")
- **Mirror as price-objection handler:** "the price is too high" → "too high?" (up-inflection) → they explain and reveal the competitor quote (Matt Macnamara — "Never Split the Difference 3 SALES Tips")
- **Label to defuse tension mid-deal:** "Chris, it seems like you think I'm being a bit unfair here" — opened the prospect up during a stalled POC (Matt Macnamara — "Never Split the Difference 3 SALES Tips")
- **Tone-mismatch probe:** when they agree but the tone is off — "You seemed a bit hesitant when I asked that," then stay silent to draw out the real concern (Matt Macnamara — "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice")
- **Label the miss:** when copy/pitch lands flat — "Sounds like I missed the mark somewhere. Would you be kind enough to explain where, in a bit more detail?" (Matt Macnamara — "LIVE Role Playing Sales Objections")
- **Answer a question with a question** — only answer once you understand the motive: "Are you saying that even if you believed what I do would work, you couldn't hire me because I lack [X]?" gets them to dismantle their own objection (Matt Macnamara — "BRILLIANT Sales Objection Handling Advice")
- **Don't accept the first "no":** ask follow-ups to surface the *real* reason; once you understand every reason you can often flip it (Frank Bettger) (Matt Macnamara — "After Reading 40 Books on Sales")
- **Disqualify-to-close:** "If it's not the right fit, that's okay — invite yourself out and introduce them to someone better." Selling a bad-fit product burns future chances (Iannarino) (Matt Macnamara — "After Reading 40 Books on Sales")
- **Don't steamroll with a slick close:** acknowledge first ("I hear you"), ask 1-2 questions to understand what they need to think about, THEN respond; present both possible objections and let them pick rather than removing one for them (Matt Macnamara — "Tech Sales Pro Reacts to Andy Elliot")
- **Graceful exit after repeated no's:** "Sounds like three strikes, I'm out — thank you for my shot. Would it be all right if I checked back in a month or two?" then keep warm with value-add emails ("came across this article on realtors using AI to save 10 hrs/week, thought of you") (Matt Macnamara — "Reacting to the GREATEST Cold Call ever made")
- **IOI vs brush-off on "send me an email":** an IOI sounds like "send that, I've got two people I'll share it with" — move to close; a genuine brush-off → accept but plant a seed ("hit reply with any key so I know a human saw it — would it be awful if I circled back in 2-3 weeks?") - **"Commission breath"** (Josh Braun): don't be so attached to the outcome — the prospect hears it in your tone (Matt Macnamara — "The BEST Cold Call Objection Handling Training")
- **Interview self-as-product close:** "Based on today, anything holding you back from moving me forward?" → "So it sounds like I'm moving forward — walk me through next steps, and what can I do to best prepare?" (Matt Macnamara — "Mock Tech Sales Interview with Unemployed AE")
- **Interview "did you hit quota" reframe (missed):** own it, never lie, give context, emphasize team stack-rank ("60% of the team finished below 50%, I finished 3rd of 12; here are 3 things I'd change") (Matt Macnamara — "Mock Tech Sales Interview with Unemployed AE")

### Frameworks / formulas
