### Frameworks / formulas
- **OPS-CTA-PS cold email**: Observation (light research) → Problem (shared pain) → Solution/benefit → simple CTA ("worth a conversation?") → PS = a one-to-one human detail so it "screams it was only written to you." Sourced 73 meetings in 2022 (Trent Dressel — "Brian LaManna x Trent Dressel...").
- **Cold email body**: ~500 chars (tweet-length); who you are / why you're reaching out / the value (compelling event) / one CTA, with line breaks so it passes the eye test on a phone (Trent Dressel — "This Cold Email Subject Line Is A CHEAT CODE").
- **5 cold-email best practices**: subject = first name + topic; slim mobile body; personalize first sentence; follow up ("80% of sales need 5+ follow-ups"); best send ≈ Tue/Thu ~10am (Trent Dressel — "The 5 Best Practices of Cold Emailing").
- **If/Then hook formula** (Craig Clemens): "If [audience's challenge/desire], then [your product as solution]" — e.g. "If you aspire to shave 5-10 strokes off your golf score, then heed these four secrets" (_Curated Videos — "Hook Point (audiobook) — Brendan Kane").
- **5 steps to craft a hook point**: conciseness · authenticity (not clickbait) · challenge perceptions · keep it simple to grasp · spark curiosity (_Curated Videos — "Hook Point (audiobook) — Brendan Kane").
- **4 hook-point strategies**: shatter expectations · clarify the value proposition · articulate the worry that keeps them up at night better than they can · use the if-then problem-solving premise (_Curated Videos — "Hook Point (summary) — Brendan Kane").
- **PCM (Process Communication Model)** — tailor to 6 styles: Thinker (logic/data), Persister (values), Harmonizer (emotion), Imaginer (reflection), Rebel (playful), Promoter (results); appeal to hearts AND minds (_Curated Videos — "Hook Point (summary) — Brendan Kane").
- **Dream 100 / best buyers**: best buyers buy more, faster, more often; market only to the small best-buyer set and move them up an awareness ladder ("never heard of you → what is this company → think I've heard of them → yes I've heard of them → yes I do business with them") (_Curated Videos — "The Ultimate Sales Machine (audiobook) — Chet Holmes").
- **Buyer's Pyramid**: ~3% buying now, 7% open, then three 30% bands ("not thinking about it / think not interested / definitely not interested") — write to keep all 90% "in the stadium," not just the 3% (_Curated Videos — "The Ultimate Sales Machine (audiobook) — Chet Holmes").
- **Stadium Pitch / Core Story**: build one education-based presentation (market data + insight) you could deliver to a stadium of perfect prospects, then reuse across ads, direct mail, website (_Curated Videos — "The Ultimate Sales Machine (audiobook) — Chet Holmes").
- **Seven Steps to Every Sale**: rapport → qualify/find need → present core story → build value (create desire) → overcome objections → close → follow up (_Curated Videos — "The Ultimate Sales Machine (audiobook) — Chet Holmes").
- **Self-selling questions** (USM): "What's it costing you if you're NOT getting those dream clients?" / "Are you the type who likes to learn breakthroughs?" / "What if you could learn it then decide if it was worth the money — fair?" (_Curated Videos — "The Ultimate Sales Machine (audiobook) — Chet Holmes").
- **3-step cold call**: identify the target buyer ("who has my money," reverse-engineer what they care about) → focus on the need not the pain (drive an urgent compelling event) → make the ask for their time (Post-it: don't hang up till you ask) (Trent Dressel — "TOP 3 Cold Calling B2B Techniques as a Top Performer").
- **Cold-call opener = "The reason I'm calling you is ___"**: who you are, why you're calling THEM specifically, what you want. Full swipe: "Hey [name], this is [you] from [company], how are you?... I noticed you're VP of Sales — we work with leaders like you to increase pipeline and send win rates through the roof; any of those top of mind today?" (Trent Dressel — "Cold Calling Is Necessary").
- **Cold-call goal = sell the TIME (book the next meeting)**, not close the deal or run discovery; low-barrier ask renames "meeting" as a "health check" — "let's find 15 minutes this week" (Trent Dressel — "Cold Calling Is Necessary" / "From Salesperson to Sales Trainer").
- **"Plays of the day"** daily system: each morning ask every active opp "what one thing advances this deal today?", batch-execute in 30-40 min without context-switching; spend ~80% of the week only on advancing + creating pipeline (Trent Dressel — "Brian LaManna x Trent Dressel...").
- **"Why" laddering in discovery**: don't accept the surface ask ("improve our coaching") — ask why repeatedly to reach the strategic priority (win rate → losing market share → Series-B round) where real value lives (Trent Dressel — "Brian LaManna x Trent Dressel...").
- **Moneyball outbound funnel**: Answer ~6% → Set ~15% → Show ~80% → Convert ~90%; 1,000 calls ≈ 6.5 qualified opps — reverse-engineer activity from your target (Trent Dressel — "From Salesperson to Sales Trainer").
- **"Why now / compelling event" opener**: ask every prospect "Why did you agree to meet with me at this time?" — reveals whether they've already decided to buy (Trent Dressel — "GRANT CARDONE...").
- **Sell-the-gap**: map past (what failed → what to avoid) + present + desired future; the presentation just bridges the gap — you can't close someone on the wrong product (Trent Dressel — "GRANT CARDONE...").
- **"Seller, be sold" / conviction**: first sale is to yourself; "whoever is more convinced convinces the other"; complaining about your product un-sells you (Trent Dressel — "GRANT CARDONE...").

- **Feature→value translation**: low-level contacts buy features; for VP/C-level translate every feature into business impact (increases conversions, reduces wasted ad spend) (Trent Dressel — "Cold Calling Is Necessary").

- **Buyer-persona reverse-engineering**: org priorities → department goals → the individual's promotion goals; a director ≠ a VP even in the same department — sell to what THAT persona cares about (Trent Dressel — "6 Traits of High Performers").
- **Logic vs emotion**: people buy on emotion and justify with logic; even "$1M ROI in 5 days" loses to "this feels right, I want to work with that person" — win on feeling-seen + storytelling (Trent Dressel — "6 Traits of High Performers").
- **"Healthy tension"**: challenge the buyer; if you feel nervous to say something, that nervousness is the signal to say it (Trent Dressel — "6 Traits of High Performers").
- **"How I" not "How to"**: document your journey instead of claiming expert status — "what seems obvious to you can be gold to somebody else" (Trent Dressel — "Tech Layoffs Continue...").
- **Reciprocity-before-ask**: engage/comment on a target's content consistently → earn name recognition → only then make the ask; you can't offer or ask for value cold (Trent Dressel — "Tech Layoffs Continue...").
- **"Front door vs back door"**: front door = auto-apply into a pile of hundreds; back door = personal brand + skills + network to reach the actual decision-maker (referral-first hiring) (Trent Dressel — "7 Highest Paying Sales Jobs..." / "Land Your First Tech Sales Job in 2025").
- **Discovery checklist**: pain · decision process · decision criteria · success metric · timeline · budget · compelling event ("why now"). Sales-cycle stages: cold call → IQM → discovery → demo → negotiation → legal/finance/IT → signature (Trent Dressel — "Day In the Life of An Account Executive").
- **Build a personal objection-response swipe file**: write down every objection you hear, draft a response, ask peers what they say, keep the highest-win-rate phrases — "if you can't write down how you'd respond, you have no chance of responding on the actual phone" (Trent Dressel — "How To Overcome The Most Common Sales Objections").
- **Control-the-pace principle**: when the prospect rushes you, slow down and keep asking questions until they hang up or you've truly disqualified them (Trent Dressel — "Actual Live Cold Call Sales Training" / "TOP 3 Cold Calling...").
- **Always get the time on the calendar**: when a prospect is loose ("reconnect in a month or two"), tighten — propose a specific week, ask day + morning/afternoon, send the invite to boost show rate (Trent Dressel — "Actual Live Cold Call Sales Training").
- **10 cold-calling blocks/week**: 8-10am + 3-5pm, Mon-Fri; miss one block and you lose ~10% of total output capacity (Trent Dressel — "Cold Calling Is Necessary").
- **Aggressive multi-touch sequence**: over ~23 days, ~8-9 calls + ~8-9 emails + automated voicemails so "it's unavoidable they'll know my name"; ~80% of deals take 5-12 contacts, avg 7.6 calls before a pickup (Trent Dressel — "Is Being A Sales Development Rep Hard?" / "GRANT CARDONE...").
- **3-step rejection framework**: seek out rejection → become indifferent to it → hold supreme confidence in your future ability to produce (Trent Dressel — "10 Minutes Away From Never Caring About Rejection Again").

### Objection handling
- **Sell by not selling** (disarm): repeatedly state "I'm not trying to sell you anything, this is completely free knowledge," position competitors as wanting you to "feel inadequate so you pay," then make the soft CTA (Trent Dressel — "My Thoughts On Tech Sales Bootcamps").
- **Universal clarifier before responding to ANY objection**: "What about this doesn't work for you?" → mirror back: "So to make sure I understand, it sounds like you feel [X] is going to be a challenge." (Trent Dressel — "How To Overcome The Most Common Sales Objections" / "6 Traits...").
- **Early-call brush-off** ("send an email / call later / I'm busy"): control the pace — "Would it be fair if I call you back later? Would you have 30 seconds for me to tell you the reason I'm calling, so I don't keep following up if there's no need?" (Trent Dressel — "TOP 3 Cold Calling..." / "LIVE COLD CALL OBJECTION HANDLING").
- **End-of-call objection** ("no budget / not the time / using a competitor"): make them feel heard ("I figured you had something in place — I'm not asking for budget today"), then give a validated reason to still meet: "By the end you'll either see why we're a better fit, or feel even better about your existing solution." (Trent Dressel — "TOP 3 Cold Calling...").
- **Competitor = buying signal reframe**: a named competitor means a serious evaluation (real competitor is usually the status quo / doing nothing); always speak positively about competitors ("great tool, heard nothing but good things") and solution-sell instead of mud-slinging (Trent Dressel — "Brian LaManna x Trent Dressel..." / "How To Overcome...").
- **"Using a competitor"**: "They're a great vendor — the reason orgs typically switch to us is [XYZ]; let's talk about incremental value." If locked in a multi-year contract, don't fight it: "When do you do yearly planning? I'd like to reconnect when it makes sense." (Trent Dressel — "How To Overcome The Most Common Sales Objections").
- **"No budget"**: "I'm not actually asking for any budget right now" — humanize, acknowledge cost exists, pivot to current state + pain; reframe to outcome ("homegrown solutions are usually low-impact; that's why 13,000 customers use us... options that cost less but deliver more impact"). Isolation close: "Aside from budget, any other reservations?" (Trent Dressel — "LIVE COLD CALL OBJECTION HANDLING" / "How To Overcome...").
- **"Not the right time"**: "What about that time will be better? What needs to change between now and then?" then book it anyway and send the invite (Trent Dressel — "How To Overcome The Most Common Sales Objections").
- **"I don't need your solution"**: agitate cost of inaction — "Here are the negative consequences other customers face from NOT having our product." (Trent Dressel — "How To Overcome...").
- **Status-quo / make-them-uncomfortable** (USM): "People act faster to solve a problem than to gain an unrealized benefit" — use market data + core story to surface unconsidered problems; "features tell, benefits sell." Plus Jay Abraham's moral-obligation close: "If you truly believe what you have is valuable, you have a moral obligation to help them decide." (_Curated Videos — "The Ultimate Sales Machine (audiobook) — Chet Holmes").
- **Trust/disbelief, asked directly**: "How much of what I've said do you actually believe?" — surfacing distrust de-risks the deal instead of blowing it (Trent Dressel — "GRANT CARDONE...").
- **Stalled deal / no next step**: "It sounds like this is what we're trying to accomplish — do you not feel it's worth your time to continue?" / "If you went back to your team right now, would we be your recommendation?" (a non-definitive yes = red flag) (Trent Dressel — "GRANT CARDONE...").
- **Challenge an instant "not interested"**: "What about this doesn't work for you? I haven't even told you our solution — you don't know who I am and you've already written us off." (Trent Dressel — "6 Traits of High Performers").
- **Service-not-selling reframe for call reluctance**: "You're not convincing anyone to do something they don't want — you're in service of them, letting them know about a problem they may not be aware of." (Trent Dressel — "Cold Calling Is Necessary").
- **Acknowledge-comply-pivot on "send me an email"**: "Yeah, I'd love to — is it Trent@google.com? Great." Recognize, make them feel heard, then re-pivot to the meeting ask (Trent Dressel — "Cold Calling Is Necessary").
- **Reframe "no" itself**: "Just because somebody tells you no doesn't mean they're not interested — never look at rejection as a dead end, just a new obstacle." Abundance reframe: "There are 8 billion people — if I get rejected, there are still billions of others I could talk to." (Trent Dressel — "10 Minutes Away From Never Caring About Rejection Again").
- **AI-will-replace-this**: "AI will replace a lot of jobs, but we need people to sell the AI — a Fortune 500 won't sign a $10M license without speaking to a human." (Trent Dressel — "Why Tech Sales Is The Best Career In 2025").
- **"No degree / wrong background"**: reframe as advantage — "If you don't have a degree, that's even better... all that matters is performance, not your last name, looks, degree, or who you know." (Trent Dressel — "Tech Sales: The Exciting Career...").
- **Disengagement tell**: when you ask "how are you?" and they say "good" without asking back, that's the signal they don't want the call — get to the point fast (Trent Dressel — "Actual Live Cold Call Sales Training").

- Universal move: restate the objection calmly, then "What about this doesn't work for you? Why?" — keep going layers deep to the root cause before giving up. (Trent Dressel — "The Best Cold Call Script For Any Product")
- Competitor-under-contract → get the renewal date, then "3 months before renewal you'll re-evaluate — let's set a brief call then." Don't set a pointless meeting if they're locked in. (Trent Dressel — "Common Cold Calling Objections & Best Responses To Use")
- Walk-away leverage: "The person willing to walk away has the most leverage." Enter every deal able to NOT close and you carry confidence instead of quota-breath. (Trent Dressel — "Common Cold Calling Objections & Best Responses To Use")

### Objection handling
- **30-second permission ask (disarm a rushed prospect):** "May I have 30 seconds to tell you the reason why I called?" / "If the call feels rushed, it's YOU who's rushing it." (Trent Dressel — "Live Cold Calling Until They Accept My Meeting" / "MY CAREER IS PLUMMETING LIVE COLD CALLING")
- **"Too expensive / over budget" reframe:** don't accept the no — "Do we have an opportunity to meet you on your budget?" (Trent Dressel — "Tech Sales Is Not A Stable Career")
- **"Moving in another direction" reframe:** "Based on our conversations I think we're a great fit… what am I missing?" (Trent Dressel — "Tech Sales Is Not A Stable Career")
- **Gatekeeper peer-to-peer reframe:** "I know with him being in sales, I'm also in sales — I'm sure he's an advocate of cold calls for his team... we're just looking for a partnership." (Trent Dressel — "MY CAREER IS PLUMMETING LIVE COLD CALLING")
- **Gatekeeper "I'll have to ask my boss" pivot:** "I figured that was the case — that's exactly why I'm reaching out. Let me send a follow-up; I'll CC [boss], could you make sure he sees it?" (Trent Dressel — "How To Get Past The Gatekeeper")
- **Wrong-person redirect (gracious + referral):** "Maybe my records are outdated... I was hoping to reach whoever oversees [category] — do you know who that might be?" (Trent Dressel — "MY CAREER IS PLUMMETING" / "Live Cold Calling Until They Accept My Meeting")
- **Competitor objection (don't get defensive):** "They're a great company — I encourage you to check them out. Is there anything other vendors have shown you that's really stood out?" (Trent Dressel — "The Most Powerful Sales Questions MEDDICCC")
- **Competitor-under-contract:** get the renewal date, set a brief call ~3 months before renewal; don't book a pointless meeting if they're locked in (Trent Dressel — "Common Cold Calling Objections")
- **No-urgency / "send a proposal and we'll circle back":** urgency only exists if negative consequences of inaction were established and agreed BEFORE the proposal — no agreed pain = stalled deal (Trent Dressel — "The Software Sales Fundamentals")
- **Change-risk reframe:** "Any change includes risk; unless the current state is really uncomfortable, it's not comfortable to take on that risk" — surface status-quo pain to justify switching (Trent Dressel — "The Software Sales Fundamentals")
- **Influencer → economic buyer:** make the individual win first ("how do I get this person promoted/paid/looking good?"), then "Help me understand, from your VP's perspective, why is this program failing them?" (Trent Dressel — "The Software Sales Fundamentals")
- **Show-up-with-a-viewpoint (call reluctance):** "You don't need to know what to say — make the call, figure it out later. Say: this is what I hear from other leaders, this is what you should care about, this is how we help — interested?" (Trent Dressel — "How To Approach Customers In Sales")
- **No-show / no-reply reframe:** stop saying what YOU want ("I don't want to get no-showed") — reframe every message through "what value am I providing them?" (Trent Dressel — "How To Become Best SDR Within Year 1")
- **Tentative-yes-to-firm-commitment:** when they say "connect later," send a tentative calendar placeholder with your number to lock the next step (Trent Dressel — "Live Cold Calling Until They Accept My Meeting")
- **No-brainer cost-of-labor reframe:** "You need to hire three people for this? Maybe just use our software — more leverage, more scale, less low-level admin." (Trent Dressel — "How To SELL During a Recession")
- **Rejection reframe (resilience):** "I'm one 'no' away from a 'yes'" / "the more I get rejected, the more I want to take action to reach that yes." (Trent Dressel — "Life As SDR: The Ugly Truth" / "How To Become The Best SDR")
- **"Burnout" rebuttal:** "Burnout doesn't exist — it's a misalignment between your purpose, your why, and what you actually focus on." (Trent Dressel — "Why You Don't COLD CALL Enough")
- **"Layoffs" objection (applying to a company that cut staff):** "Every company does layoffs. If you were in a position to be laid off, you weren't in a leadership position — everyone's replaceable, but they'll pay you a lot of money." (Trent Dressel — "Top 10 Tech Companies Hiring")
- **Voicemail value-lead (cost-savings angle):** "all we're looking for is an opportunity to see if we can save [company] cost on items your reps take to market... increase margin on like-for-like items." (Trent Dressel — "MY CAREER IS PLUMMETING LIVE COLD CALLING")
- **Walk-away leverage:** "The person willing to walk away has the most leverage." Enter able to NOT close and you carry confidence instead of quota-breath. (Trent Dressel — "Common Cold Calling Objections" / "How to get into Software Sales")

### Frameworks / formulas
- 4-question value-build: "What are you doing today? What about it isn't working? What do you want this to work like? Why does this matter?" — surfaces before-state, pain, after-state, business outcome. (Trent Dressel — "Top 4 Sales Techniques To WIN More")
- Goal-setting 5 questions: "What do you want? What's important about it? How will you get it? What's preventing you? How will you know when you have it?" (Trent Dressel — "Top 4 Sales Techniques To WIN More")
- Cold call 3-step: (1) clear reason why you're calling + what you want, (2) lead with value (make money / save money / mitigate risk), (3) make the ask for time. (Trent Dressel — "The B2B Cold Call Scripts That Actually Book Meetings")
- Opener formula: "Hey [Name], this is [You] from [Company]. The reason I called is I noticed you're the [title] and we help groups like yours [outcome A] and [outcome B] — is either a priority this year?" (ask an obvious yes-question). (Trent Dressel — "The B2B Cold Call Scripts That Actually Book Meetings")
- "No-strings partnership" pre-empt: "I know you're not looking to change today / no budget / under contract — but there'll come a time you're back in market. I'd like to share ideas you can use today, no strings... would you be opposed to that?" (Trent Dressel — "The B2B Cold Call Scripts That Actually Book Meetings")
- Ask-then-pause: one question (no double-barreling), then silence — the second thing the prospect says is more valuable than the first. (Trent Dressel — "11 Sales Mistakes to Avoid in 2022")
- Discovery decision-criteria Qs: "On your wish list of a dream solution, what are the must-have items?" / "What would be most important to a successful program?" (Trent Dressel — "11 Sales Mistakes to Avoid in 2022")
- PREDICT qualification: Problem (w/ pain), Reason (personal + company why), Engagement (multi-thread + responsiveness), Decision maker/process, Impact (4 levels: individual/users/company/customer), Cost (current/opportunity/proposal), Timeline (compelling event + go-live). (Ian Koniak — "PREDICT SELLING")
- Sell the gap, not the sticker: position price against what they already pay (ask $1M but they retire $700K of tools = "only asking $300K"). (Ian Koniak — "PREDICT SELLING")
- Three components of cost to uncover: current cost (people + software + outsourcing), opportunity cost (growth they can't do), proposal cost (budget/funding). (Ian Koniak — "PREDICT SELLING")
- Trusted-advisor move: become the expert on the *problem* (and why it's a problem), not just the product — "the problem isn't a problem until they feel the pain." (Ian Koniak — "Become a Trusted Advisor")
- The 100% Commitment Close: never concede on price until prospect is 100% committed and price is the *only* obstacle. Isolate: "If I could make the finances work, would you be 100% in? Is that the only thing stopping you?" (Ian Koniak — "My #1 negotiation tip to close big deals")
- "If money were not an option, what would you want?" — gets prospect to name true (higher-tier) desire before negotiating. (Ian Koniak — "My #1 negotiation tip to close big deals")
- Brian Tracy 7-step system: 1) Prospecting (qualify), 2) Rapport/trust, 3) Questioning/needs, 4) Presentation (the sale is made here), 5) Answer objections, 6) Close, 7) Follow-up → referrals. (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Brian Tracy")
- "Doctor of selling" frame: Examination → Diagnosis → Prescription. "Based on what you've told me, I'd recommend..." (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Brian Tracy")
- Law of Probabilities: double new contacts (2→4 calls/day) and you double sales. (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Brian Tracy")
- "Be interested, not interesting" — ask questions, listen, take visible notes; opener "How did you get into this business anyway?" then "And then what did you do?" (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Brian Tracy")
- Three sales in every customer: 1st (hardest), 2nd (repeat, earned by service), 3rd (the referral — free). (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Brian Tracy")

### Objection handling
- Salvage a botched call by naming it: "I get the sense I really missed the mark today. My intention is to coordinate a follow-up to discuss what you care about and how we can help — what do you say?" (Trent Dressel — "The B2B Cold Call Scripts")
- Don't accept a flat "no" — dig past the excuse to the real blocker, reaffirm value, then ask "what's it going to take to get this done?" (Trent Dressel — "11 Sales Mistakes")
- Reframe "deal is closed": it isn't closed until there's a signature — keep closing, "like a ball game, until the clock hits zero the game is never over." (Trent Dressel — "11 Sales Mistakes")
- Overcome status-quo inertia by educating on the *problem* — most buyers don't realize what they do today is a big problem; lead from knowledge, not emotion. (Ian Koniak — "Become a Trusted Advisor")
- Justify higher price by quantifying current spend so the ask becomes "just the gap," making the investment feel small. (Ian Koniak — "PREDICT SELLING")
- Money objection reframe: "Money should never be the obstacle that stops somebody from working with you if you're the right solution" — isolate, find the real constraint (cash flow vs term vs funding), then solve it. (Ian Koniak — "My #1 negotiation tip")
- Don't lead with discounts: "Too many people lead with money, lead with discounts, and wonder why the client doesn't buy" — validate commitment first. (Ian Koniak — "My #1 negotiation tip")
- Respect-the-objection script: "That's a good question. Thank you for asking. Let me see if I can answer it." — never call it an objection; treat as a question. (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Brian Tracy")
- Price objection rebuttal: "Nobody buys on the basis of price — they buy on the benefit they expect. Price is a factor; it's never the reason." Proof: "Anyone here buy a single item solely because it was the cheapest?" (silence). (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Brian Tracy")
- Skeptic rebuttal (low-risk trial): "Why don't you give it a try before you dismiss it? It doesn't cost anything. I'm not asking you for money." (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Brian Tracy")
- Trust-before-pitch reframe: "People won't buy even if you have the cheapest, best product — they won't buy until they like you," and they like you when you ask questions. (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Brian Tracy")
- Reframe imposter syndrome as proof of growth: "A touch of imposter syndrome means you're reaching — putting yourself in bigger rooms." (Ian Koniak — "The Conversation Every Top Seller NEEDS to hear")
- "Not qualified / don't belong" reframe: the belief is "your truth" but "doesn't serve you" and physically drains energy; choose the upside ("I get to figure this out"). (Ian Koniak — "Episode 6")
- Walk away to win: "We can't participate — this RFP isn't written for you to succeed, and here's why" → prospects stop the RFP and go sole-source. (Ian Koniak — "He sold 1.2 BILLION")
- "You're not a player in the market" objection → escalate over the buyer: had own CEO call their CIO; turned a flat no into a $2.5M/yr win in 90 days. (Ian Koniak — "He sold 1.2 BILLION")
- No executive sponsorship = no deal: "If it's not a priority to an executive, it's not going to happen. Go to the top first or don't work the deal." (Ian Koniak — "The Conversation Every Top Seller NEEDS to hear")
- Pain over gain: buyers ~7x more likely to move to alleviate pain than chase gain — "they don't believe the gain story anymore, so you've got to fix something." (Ian Koniak — "He sold 1.2 BILLION")
- Detach to disarm price/neediness: know your runway so you "don't have to take bad clients or bad deals" — scarcity energy repels, service energy attracts. (Ian Koniak — "Detach to Win")
- "Too disruptive / too much change" → present an implementation plan where you do the legwork and spell out minimal exact internal time ("a PM at 25%, exec sponsor 2 hrs/week") so they have certainty. (Ian Koniak — "What's the #1 reason Enterprise Customers choose not to buy?")
- "No urgency" → quantify cost of waiting, throw their own number back: "You agreed every month you wait costs ~$100k — what do we need to do to get this done?" (Ian Koniak — "What's the #1 reason Enterprise Customers choose not to buy?")
- "Loved the demo but went silent" → it's not lack of interest or budget; they're busy keeping the lights on and lose momentum. Most customers "don't know how to buy" — do that work for them. (Ian Koniak — "What's the #1 reason Enterprise Customers choose not to buy?")
- "I can't spend that money" → "You're the asset; nobody doubles their income on their own — you need an accelerator" (reframes price as the cost of staying stuck). (Ian Koniak — "Episode 1")
- "I just need tactics, my mindset is fine" → the real lever is identity/beliefs: "If you don't change your identity to be an elite seller, you'll never act like one." (Ian Koniak — "Episode 1")
- "Watching videos/podcasts is enough" → information alone doesn't create growth; accountability "usually comes in the form of a paid engagement." (Ian Koniak — "Elite Sales Performer Trait #9")

- "The Proposal Template that helped me close $100M" — number-anchored, result-in-title: specific tool ("template") + massive specific number. (Ian Koniak — "The Proposal Template that helped me close $100M")
- "Do this one Revenue-Generating Activity to win 62% of your deals." — stat-backed promise hook (top 20% of sellers close 62% of deals that reach proposal). (Ian Koniak — "Do this Revenue Generating Activity to win 62% of your deals")
- "She sold $15 million in less than 6 months after transforming herself, then quit her job." — proof + curiosity gap + reversal. (Ian Koniak — "Episode 4 She sold 15M in 5 months at AWS")
- "He Made Millions in Tech Sales — Then Retired to Sail the World with His Family" — identity + dream-outcome + proof structure. (Ian Koniak — "He Made Millions in Tech Sales — Then Retired to Sail the World with His Family")
- "He sold $87M at 34 years old" — age + dollar-figure proof hook for a case-study/interview title. (Ian Koniak — "Episode 7 - He sold 87M at 34 years old")
- "I hit quota 42 months in a row — selling copiers up and down the streets of LA." — streak + humble-origin proof. (Ian Koniak — "The Science of Selling")
- "It's not important if customers believe what you're saying. What's more important is that they believe YOU believe what you're saying." (Ian Koniak — "The 2 traits that every #1 tech seller shares")
- "They're more afraid of messing up than they are of missing out." — loss-aversion reframe for why buyers stall. (Ian Koniak — "3 Strategies for Overcoming Customer Indecision")
- "You can't sell to somebody who can't say yes." — punchy authority/qualification line. (Ian Koniak — "Do this Revenue Generating Activity to win 62% of your deals")
- "When you want to sell, you repel. When you just serve, people lean in." — antithesis one-liner. (Ian Koniak — "How to Escape a Scarcity Mindset")
- "Those who care the least win the most." / "The more worried about your job, the more likely you are to lose it." — paradox hooks. (Ian Koniak — "How to Escape a Scarcity Mindset")
- "Those who pay, pay attention." — rhyming line justifying paid offers over free content. (Ian Koniak — "How to Escape a Scarcity Mindset")
- "People don't pay for information — information is free. What people pay for is application." — swipe-able line for any coaching/done-with-you offer. (Ian Koniak — "7 steps to build your side hustle coaching business")
- "It's not about how hard you work, it's about what you're working on when you're working." — reframe hook. (Ian Koniak — "How to work less and make more $$$ in sales (RGA's)")
- "Be interested, not interesting." — memorable opener for relationship-led selling. (Ian Koniak — "Which sales methodology is best")
- "Done now always beats perfect later — or perfect never." — punchy CTA-closer. (Ian Koniak — "Perfectionism kills productivity!")
- "Do what others won't do today so you can do what others can't do tomorrow." — aspirational sacrifice line. (Ian Koniak — "Can Money Buy Happiness")
- "Work will not be as loyal as your family will." — emotional gut-punch line. (Ian Koniak — "How to balance work and family life")
- "Just because you make more doesn't mean you have to increase your cost of living." (Ian Koniak — "How to Build Wealth in Sales")
- "If you build it, they will come — but only if they know who you are." — twist on a famous line; closer for audience-first launches. (Ian Koniak — "7 steps to build your side hustle coaching business")
- "You guys are a band of bandits… misfits who've overcome a lot of adversity and just want to get better." — identity/belonging hook for the ICP. (Ian Koniak — "Untap Your Sales Potential Podcast Trailer")
- "Commission breath — customers will sense it." — visceral, memorable phrase; usable as hook or section header. (Ian Koniak — "He Made Millions in Tech Sales…")
- "If it scares you, that's the exact reason you need this — because then you'll actually do the work." (Ian Koniak — "Which Coaching Membership Level is right for me?")

### Frameworks / formulas
- **The Story Mountain (proposal narrative arc):** Exposition (customer as hero + their vision/goals) → Rising Action (their pain, twist the knife) → Climax (your solution as the helper) → Falling Action (investment, ROI/business case, rollout) → Resolution (mutual action plan / next steps). Customer is the hero; "the story is about them, not you." (Ian Koniak — "The Proposal Template that helped me close $100M")
- **The Killer Proposal Template (slide sequence):** Team/shared journey → Vision & goals → Challenges & pain (with discovery quotes, esp. negative) → "common problem" tension-easer + industry research → Exec summary → Solution/demo → Investment → Business case/ROI → Implementation & training plan → Architecture/future state OR customer story → Next steps / mutual action plan. Bonus: use the CUSTOMER'S OWN deck template so it reads neutral, not vendor-authored. (Ian Koniak — "The Proposal Template that helped me close $100M")
- **Yo-Yo Selling (enterprise discovery):** Start high (C-suite) → secure executive sponsorship → go down to meet their teams → collect info, go wide across departments → come back up with business case, custom demo, implementation plan, proposal. (Ian Koniak — "Stop Selling Software. Sell Discovery Instead." / "He Made Millions in Tech Sales…")
- **Sell the discovery process, not the solution** — map 4 things to win the next step: (1) WHO else you need to meet + why, (2) WHAT you need to see (e.g. full "lead to cash" process), (3) the DELIVERABLES, (4) HOW LONG + exact time commitment. (Ian Koniak — "Stop Selling Software. Sell Discovery Instead.")
- **Ghostwrite the handoff email** — after getting sponsorship, draft (via AI) the intro email the exec sends their team, get cc'd, then "come over the top" to schedule directly. Converts cold internal asks into warm referrals. (Ian Koniak — "Stop Selling Software. Sell Discovery Instead.")
- **The Science of Selling (reverse-math quota formula):** Annual quota ÷ 12 = monthly → ÷ avg deal size = deals/mo → ÷ close ratio = opps needed → ÷ appt-to-opp ratio = appts needed → ÷ contact-to-appt ratio = daily activity. Worked: $1.2M/yr → $100K/mo → 4 deals ($25K) → 16 opps (25% close) → 40 appts/mo → 10/wk → 2/day. (Ian Koniak — "The Science of Selling")
- **"Do 2, Set 2" activity model:** 2 appointments done + 2 set daily = 10/week → ~4 opps → 1 close at 25%. Measure OUTPUTS (appointments set), not inputs (cold calls). (Ian Koniak — "The Science of Selling" / "Elite Sales Performer Trait #8 FAITH")
- **The 4 RGAs (Revenue Generating Activities):** (1) Set appointments, (2) Prep for meetings, (3) Do meetings, (4) Follow up. "Everything else is noise." (Variant: 3 RGAs = create pipeline / advance pipeline / **re-qualify pipeline** — the third is the one nobody does and why deals stall.) (Ian Koniak — "How to work less and make more $$$ (RGA's)" / "Do this Revenue Generating Activity to win 62% of your deals")
- **The 4 P's of qualifying:** Pain, Priority, Power, Process. "Better to have 7 real deals with power/priority/pain than 15-20 that aren't real." (Ian Koniak — "Do this Revenue Generating Activity to win 62% of your deals")
- **Three questions that make a deal qualified:** Why change (quantified cost of inaction), Why now (urgency, or it gets deprioritized), Why you (what's unique about your solution to deliver in the time needed). (Ian Koniak — "Do this Revenue Generating Activity to win 62% of your deals")
- **The 2 timeless traits of #1 sellers:** (1) Belief — "sales is a transference of belief" (in self, process, product); (2) Authenticity — "nobody else can do you, so you should do you." Corollary: Trust > Like — they don't even have to like you; trust (belief you'll do right by them) beats style mismatch. (Ian Koniak — "The 2 traits that every #1 tech seller shares")
- **Executive-sponsor "balls and strikes" play:** Ask "Who's your executive sponsor for this project?" → educate that a cross-functional deal needs someone above the fray "to call balls and strikes and keep us moving" → get introduced 1–2 levels above where competitors are stuck → set a recurring exec cadence. Credited with a 75% win rate. (Ian Koniak — "The 2 traits that every #1 tech seller shares")
- **Champion activation sequence:** Isolate the objection BEFORE hearing it → confirm it's the ONLY thing → surface the hidden real objection → reframe → re-confirm they feel good → only then handle the external blocker (spouse/boss/board). A champion who isn't 100% convinced can't sell internally. (Ian Koniak — "The #1 question you must ask your champion")
- **Consumption/farming-rep discovery playbook:** (a) audit what they use vs. don't in your product, (b) ask "What are you doing OUTSIDE [product] that you could do INSIDE it?" → consolidate scattered tools into one place. Turned $100/mo deals into $350/mo. (Ian Koniak — "Episode 7 - He sold 87M at 34 years old")
- **Consultant vs. seller positioning:** a seller does "show and tell" (product does the work); a consultant has no product, must "show you can be helpful." Mantra: "At your service." Earn the right to prescribe (doctor metaphor — don't prescribe after two symptoms). Then "broaden the scope": start at the narrow ask, ladder up to goals/org/bigger initiative to reach power. (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Noah Flower: How to Sell Like a Consultant")
- **The IAN selling method:** Interested (not interesting) → Authentic (make any method your own; don't follow a script) → Need (uncover need for career/role success, not just product need). Frame as "human to human (H2H)." (Ian Koniak — "Which sales methodology is best")
- **Gap Selling (Keenan), endorsed:** map current state → future state → quantify the gap and its cost → bridge with your product. (Ian Koniak — "Which sales methodology is best")
- **3-pillar transformation system:** Mindset → Habits → Skills. Repeated big idea: "I didn't do it by learning tactics. I had to transform who I was." (Ian Koniak — "Untap Your Sales Potential Trailer" / "7 steps…")
- **7-step side-hustle/coaching build:** (1) Identify your unique differentiator, (2) Define ICP = the prior version of yourself, (3) Decide what to teach, (4) Build curriculum (modules → digestible lessons), (5) Choose delivery/product, (6) Teach to build an audience FIRST, (7) Build the product last. (Ian Koniak — "7 steps to build your side hustle coaching business")
- **ICP = "the prior version of yourself"** — "Talk to the version of you from a few years ago who needed help." Powerful IVOC-targeting shortcut. (Ian Koniak — "7 steps to build your side hustle coaching business")
- **ChatGPT prospecting-email refinement loop:** generic draft → add prospect's top challenges → make challenges specific (not "develop strategies/manage teams") → request bullets (challenge + how you solve it) → personalize to industry → personalize to named company + tie their public goals to your offer. Principle: "The best prospecting emails are all about the customer, the personas, and the challenges they face" — not about you. (Ian Koniak — "How to Use Chat GPT for e-mail Prospecting")
- **Parkinson's Law as a productivity lever:** "Work expands to fill the time allotted." Give yourself less time → forced efficiency. "Treat yourself like an executive." Calendar-first balance: block personal calendar (vacations, date nights, workouts) months ahead, build work around it. (Ian Koniak — "How to work less and make more $$$" / "How to balance work and family life")
- **"Action is the antidote to perfectionism":** reframe — perfectionists believe "I must be competent to act"; winners believe "action will make me competent." (Ian Koniak — "Perfectionism kills productivity!")
- **Faith-building formula (selling under uncertainty):** Know what you want (measurable goal + deep why) → learn from someone who's done it → create the plan → trust the process & execute daily ("focus on the process, not the prize") → patience. "Not blind faith — faith in a plan." (Ian Koniak — "Elite Sales Performer Trait #8 FAITH")
- **Competence ladder (beats imposter syndrome):** unconscious incompetence → conscious incompetence → conscious competence → unconscious competence; close the gap with practice + calendar-blocked routines. (Ian Koniak — "How to Gain Confidence and Overcome Imposter Syndrome")
- **RAD goal-setting:** R = Reason (strong why), A = Ambitious (forces change), D = Drastic action (sustained). Built across ~10 life categories. Paired reframe (Alex Kremer): "The purpose of a goal is not to achieve it — it's who it requires you to become to get there." (Ian Koniak — "My 2025 RAD Goals" / "My RAD goals for 2024")
- **4 wealth-building moves in tech sales:** (1) Get great at ONE thing ("make the main thing the main thing"), (2) Live within your means, (3) Passively invest consistently (index + real estate), (4) Start a side business at $400–500K+ income for tax leverage. (Ian Koniak — "Top 4 ways to build wealth in tech sales")
- **"State → Story → Strategy"** (Mike Feerick): the state you're in drives the story you tell yourself, which drives the strategy you run. "Qualities lead to tactics, not the other way around." (Ian Koniak — "He Made Millions in Tech Sales…")

### VOC language
- "I've been doing well but I know there's another level — I just don't know how to get there." (Ian Koniak — "Which Coaching Membership Level is right for me?")
- "Why not me? What are they doing differently that I'm not doing?" — internal monologue of the prospect watching peers win 2–4x. (Ian Koniak — "Untap Your Sales Potential Trailer" / "Which Coaching Membership Level…")
- "I felt like a loser. I felt like a failure. I didn't even know who I was." — raw failure-state after missing quota 3 years. (Ian Koniak — "Untap Your Sales Potential Trailer")
- "Is this it? Is this all I have in my life — just money?" / "How long can I be on this hamster wheel of sales — 10, 15, 20 years?" (Ian Koniak — "Which Coaching Membership Level is right for me?")
- "I don't know what is missing, but I'm not truly happy. I know life can offer more. I know there's more meant for me." (target: 25–45, chased money/status, feels hollow). (Ian Koniak — "The Life Success Formula")
- Scarcity spiral (verbatim): "I made 500K this year but what if it doesn't work… I'm worried I got lucky… what if they take away my territory… what if macro conditions make our product less effective." (Ian Koniak — "The #1 question you must ask your champion")
- "I feel like an impostor. I want to make sure I don't lose this opportunity. How do I keep [this income] as my standard?" (Ian Koniak — "The #1 question you must ask your champion")
- Imposter self-talk: "I got lucky," "it was accidental," "I'm not good enough, not smart enough, I don't belong." (Ian Koniak — "How to Gain Confidence and Overcome Imposter Syndrome")
- Achiever pain: "No matter how much money you're making, how successful you are, you still feel like you're never doing enough" — guilt/shame that follows you to weekends and family. (Ian Koniak — "The Achievers Dilemma")
- "I should just end this. If I can't make money, I'm worthless." / "I was making money by God, instead of making my priorities my priorities." — high-achiever burnout. (Ian Koniak — "Episode 4 She sold 15M in 5 months at AWS")
- Buyer fear (decision risk): "It's their neck on the line" — won't get fired for doing nothing, could get fired for a multi-million-dollar bet that fails. (Ian Koniak — "3 Strategies for Overcoming Customer Indecision")
- Burned-before language: "maybe they were burned in the past," "they didn't get the ROI a vendor promised," "over-promised and under-delivered," fear of "shelfware / paying for stuff they can't consume." (Ian Koniak — "3 Strategies for Overcoming Customer Indecision")
- Deal-dismissal language: "nice to have versus a must-have"; deals get "parked," "pushed," "deprioritized," "you're getting ghosted." (Ian Koniak — "Do this Revenue Generating Activity to win 62% of your deals")
- Pain isn't called "pain" — buyers say "a bottleneck," "a constraint," "a problem preventing them from achieving their goals." (Ian Koniak — "Do this Revenue Generating Activity…")
- Buyer-fear VOC (2026/AI era): "Is AI going to replace me?… we can build some of this ourselves now… there are new niche players we can use" — more options, more confusion, more risk-aversion. (Ian Koniak — "How to Escape a Scarcity Mindset")
- Status-quo objection language: "So what? Who cares? We're the leader in our market, we don't need to do anything." (Ian Koniak — "He Made Millions in Tech Sales…")
- Discovery question that surfaces dream outcomes: "What do you need to accomplish to be successful in your role?" → "grow sales by 30%," "improve our NPS / customer experience." (Ian Koniak — "Which sales methodology is best")
- Money-pain triggers worth mirroring: the $7K surprise car/brake repair ("this was my vacation money"), the full-time mom "going crazy" with no help, can't afford a plane ticket for a family funeral. (Ian Koniak — "Can Money Buy Happiness")
- Dream-outcome money language: "It enables you to do what you want, when you want, with who you want… not worrying can I take my kids to private school, can I go on this vacation." (Ian Koniak — "How to Build Wealth in Sales")
- ADHD "dread" language: "The dread is way more painful than the actual act of doing it" / "it feels like my arms are tied behind my back." (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Ian Tenenbaum ADHD Sales Mastery")
- Shame self-talk inventory: "I'm not living up to my potential," "I'm a loser" — imposter syndrome, perfectionism, procrastination all framed as "forms of shame." (Ian Koniak — "Live without Shame and Build True Confidence")

### Offers / pricing / guarantees
- **3-tier coaching ladder ("Untap Your Sales Potential," 1-yr program, positioned as "an annual MBA for sales people"):** Bronze $3,000/yr (DIY portal + courses, no live access) → Silver $9,000/yr ("do it as a group": 2 live group calls/wk, recordings, community, accountability pods) → Gold $18,000/yr ("do it WITH me": 12 one-on-ones/yr sales+life coaching, 2 in-person LA events). (Ian Koniak — "Which Coaching Membership Level is right for me?")
- **Scarcity / urgency architecture:** only 15 Gold + 50 Silver spots; "Gold sold out in two days last time"; 1,441 on the waitlist; "very little spots for a lot of people — sign up immediately." (Ian Koniak — "Which Coaching Membership Level is right for me?")
- **Pricing-justification stack:** 3-payment plan (for reps waiting on commissions); "tuition" framing (Ian's own $20K mastermind: $240K → $720K avg); employer education-reimbursement angle; "the rest is a tax write-off"; "pay out of pocket so you're more invested." (Ian Koniak — "Which Coaching Membership Level is right for me?")
- **Disqualifying / take-away offer:** "If you sell real estate or copiers, this isn't for you." / "If you're not going to put in the work, don't bother signing up." Raises perceived exclusivity. (Ian Koniak — "Which Coaching Membership Level is right for me?")
- **Anti-silver-bullet positioning:** "There's a lot of content out there — it just scratches the surface. You can't learn strategic selling in 10 weeks." (Ian Koniak — "Which Coaching Membership Level is right for me?")
- **High-ticket stacked anchor:** $225K/yr private 1:1; ~$25K program tier includes Lake Arrowhead stay, multiple masterminds, a year of content, weekly group meetings, bi-weekly deal rooms + office hours. Stacked deliverables justify a "big pill to swallow" price. (Ian Koniak — "The #1 question you must ask your champion")
- **Risk-reversal / guarantee reframe:** redefine the guaranteed outcome to something fully in your control — "I can't control your territory or macro conditions, but I guarantee you a playbook and knowing you did everything in your power… success = how you feel knowing you did your best." (Ian Koniak — "The #1 question you must ask your champion")
- **Guarantee (origin-story, swipeable):** "Come work for me and I'll guarantee your success — you make what you want to make. You just do whatever I tell you." Concrete: "Do this and I guarantee $50K yr1, $75K yr2, $100K+ yr3." (Ian Koniak — "Elite Sales Performer Trait #8 FAITH")
- **Lead-magnet CTA model:** free downloadable "Killer Proposal Template" + "talk to my team for free" as low-friction entry to a high-ticket offer; "untapyoursalespotential.com/podcast to book your free strategy call." (Ian Koniak — "The Proposal Template…" / "Episode 4 She sold 15M…")
- **Audience-before-product launch:** built audience on LinkedIn/YouTube ~2 years before launching; product "sold out within two days." Risk-reversal via demand-proofing, not guarantees. (Ian Koniak — "7 steps to build your side hustle coaching business")
- **Productized discovery as the enterprise "offer":** "One month total, 8 hours of your time — one half-day on-site vision workshop + four 1-hour interviews with department heads." Concrete, low-friction scoping of the next commitment. (Ian Koniak — "Stop Selling Software. Sell Discovery Instead.")
- **Creative contracting (de-risk to raise ACV):** (1) Carve-out — core/proven products on a 5-yr agreement, unproven products on a separate 1-yr with an out clause → bigger Year-1 ACV; (2) Price ramp — on a $5M deal charge $3M/$4M/$5M across yr1-3 so they pay only for what they consume (no shelfware). (Ian Koniak — "3 Strategies for Overcoming Customer Indecision")
- **Conservative ROI as risk-reversal:** let the customer plug in their own numbers; use the floor ("at minimum, expect this"), not pie-in-the-sky top-customer projections, so the case is one they can defend internally. (Ian Koniak — "3 Strategies for Overcoming Customer Indecision")
- **Land-and-expand / "start smaller":** carve off the highest-impact, fastest-to-implement piece to get in the door; keep the big deal moving in parallel — "you just get your deal sooner." (Ian Koniak — "3 Strategies for Overcoming Customer Indecision")
- **Value-anchoring move (free consultative engagement):** "We're not charging you, but a PwC-type firm would — this exercise costs $100K, $200K, $300K+." (Ian Koniak — "He Made Millions in Tech Sales…")
- **Proof/ROI stats for offers:** "75% close rate vs. 35% tech-sales average"; sample business case showed "$300K/month savings," "50% fewer service-desk tickets," "39% higher NPS"; "625+ sellers through my program in 4 years" from DocuSign/Salesforce/SAP/Workday. (Ian Koniak — "The Proposal Template…" / "Untap Your Sales Potential Trailer")
- **Income-gap qualifier as a hook into the offer:** "If your OTE is 150–350K and you're not making north of $500K, there's a problem." (Ian Koniak — "Can Money Buy Happiness")

### Objection handling
- **Isolate before you handle:** "Before we talk about how the conversation with your wife went — is this the ONLY thing stopping you, or do you have any lingering questions or concerns that give you pause?" Find the real objection (often the buyer's own scarcity, not the spouse). (Ian Koniak — "The #1 question you must ask your champion")
- **Direct-ask reframe for indecision:** "I'm sensing some hesitation, and I'd love to know where your thoughts are — do you have any concerns?" / "What would you need to feel comfortable moving forward?" Read body language, energy, tone. (Ian Koniak — "3 Strategies for Overcoming Customer Indecision")
- **"I'm too busy / I don't have time" (exec):** "I don't want you to have to be involved — I just need your team. Are you willing to sponsor this?" Counterintuitive insight: "When you get executives overly involved, the deal is LESS likely to close." Sell sponsorship + a delegated point person. (Ian Koniak — "Stop Selling Software. Sell Discovery Instead.")
- **"Enterprise deals are slow":** proof reframe — "All of my seven- or eight-figure deals took under six months — because I had an executive sponsor." (Ian Koniak — "Stop Selling Software. Sell Discovery Instead.")
- **"I can't afford it / it's intimidating":** "That is the EXACT reason you need this. When you're done you won't think twice about spending nine grand — you'll have that much more income." Reframes price objection as proof of need. (Ian Koniak — "Which Coaching Membership Level is right for me?")
- **"Should I invest in myself?":** "Don't invest in trips, crypto, or stock — invest in yourself, the best investment you'll ever make." Proof: missed quota 3 yrs → hired coach/$20K mastermind → finished #1 at Salesforce, income tripled. (Ian Koniak — "Which Coaching Membership Level is right for me?")
- **"This is just info I could Google":** "Information is free. People pay for application — how you help them apply it to THEIR situation." (Ian Koniak — "7 steps to build your side hustle coaching business")
- **"I don't know enough yet" (perfectionist stall):** "The reason you're not getting results isn't that you don't know what you're doing — it's that you're not taking action. Action builds competence." (Ian Koniak — "Perfectionism kills productivity!")
- **Spouse-as-blocker:** package testimonials to prove it's not a scam, listen to her concerns directly, reframe the purchase as "me showing up as a better husband for our family," not "me getting more sales." (Ian Koniak — "The #1 question you must ask your champion")
- **Status-quo / "we're the market leader":** → "Say that to Blockbuster." (loss-aversion via cautionary example). (Ian Koniak — "He Made Millions in Tech Sales…")
- **"Why this is a priority" reframe:** don't expect buyers to raise their hand with pain — "introduce them to a problem they may not know they had, and the pain it's causing," then develop a POV so you're the trusted advisor. (Ian Koniak — "Do this Revenue Generating Activity to win 62% of your deals")
- **Disqualify-don't-convince stance:** "I only want to work with people who want or need my help — not those I'm trying to convince. My time is super valuable." Reframes walking away as strength. (Ian Koniak — "Do this Revenue Generating Activity…")
- **Power test as objection-surfacer:** if they won't introduce you to the exec sponsor / give access to people, data, systems → "they're not serious." That's the qualification, not a hurdle to push through. (Ian Koniak — "Do this Revenue Generating Activity…" / "The 2 traits…")
- **De-risk the buyer's decision (exec sponsor):** "You don't even have to make the RIGHT decision — half the time it'll be wrong, doesn't matter. We just have to decide to keep moving." Removes decision pressure. (Ian Koniak — "The 2 traits that every #1 tech seller shares")
- **Flexibility close:** "Be flexible, work with them — don't be stubborn about all-or-nothing or you'll lose the deal entirely." De-risk rather than push. (Ian Koniak — "3 Strategies for Overcoming Customer Indecision")
- **Qualifying-the-sponsor reframe:** get two yeses — "It sounds like a big challenge you want to solve?" "Yes." "And is this the right time?" If they dodge to "come back in 12 months," they're not a change agent — disqualify. (Ian Koniak — "He Made Millions in Tech Sales…")
- **Champion vs. gatekeeper:** Path A — build rapport so the champion brings you to the exec; break-glass Path B — go around them. Arm a solo-going champion with material pre-built in YOUR slides so it can't be filtered/diluted on the way up. (Ian Koniak — "Episode 7 - He sold 87M at 34 years old")

### Hooks / headlines / subject lines
- "It's about to get REALLY ugly in sales — get ready!" — fear-of-loss headline for an economic-uncertainty angle (Ian Koniak — "It's about to get REALLY ugly in sales - get ready!")
- "I just lost $700,000 in market value in a period of two days" — concrete-loss cold open that earns attention before the pivot (Ian Koniak — "It's about to get REALLY ugly in sales - get ready!")
- "The #1 secret to crush your sales quota" + "less time with more people = less money; more time with less people = more commission" — swipeable contrarian hook (Ian Koniak — "#1 secret to crush your sales quota")

### Frameworks / formulas
- Hyper-personalized exec email structure: (1) sincere compliment from research, (2) "you're trying to go HERE" (their stated goals), (3) "here's the challenge with how you do it today" (gap/contrast), (4) "we can bridge the gap," (5) soft CTA / "would you be open to…" (Ian Koniak — "How to Book Meetings with Senior Execs in 2025")
- Multi-channel cadence to ONE exec: ~7 emails + 3-4 calls + a video + a voice note across 10-15 touches; more outreach to FEWER people in your biggest accounts (Ian Koniak — "How to Book Meetings with Senior Execs in 2025")
- Big-deal creation: (1) find a big/urgent problem, (2) reframe value prop around it, (3) manufacture urgency, (4) go deep AND wide (map influencers not titles), (5) be the translator between your internal experts and the buyer (Ian Koniak — "Episode 3: He made $4M commissions on a single deal!")
- Three deal non-negotiables: won't work a deal without (1) executive sponsorship/power, (2) above a minimum deal size, (3) access to do deep discovery — qualify hard, win 70-80% (Ian Koniak — "Episode 3: He made $4M commissions on a single deal!")
- "Coach them how to buy": walk the buyer through a one-page buying process (kick-off → discovery/reverse demo → tech demo → proposal+business case → go-live), then ask "anything you'd add or change?" — puts you in the driver's seat (Ian Koniak — "He became a strategic seller with 4,000 accounts!")
- Incentive (not discount) sequence: talk to economic buyer → qualify timeline + buying process early in the quarter → give them an out before revealing the offer → map a mutual action plan backwards from go-live (Ian Koniak — "How to Use Incentives without Being Pushy")
- Recession selling pivot: stop selling products; sell a free "assessment" / business-value discovery that finds cost cuts, waste reduction, vendor consolidation, fast ROI (Ian Koniak — "It's about to get REALLY ugly in sales - get ready!")
- Personalization tiers: hyper-personalized (to the individual's quotes/goals) → account-level (company goals) when you can't find info on the person; for execs you MUST hyper-personalize (Ian Koniak — "How to Book Meetings with Senior Execs in 2025")
- Four Levels of Impact (discovery): ask "what will this do for YOU / your COMPANY / your USERS / your CUSTOMERS?" — sell up the chain, not to your commission (Ian Koniak — "Impact Selling: Know your Impact")
- The "Yo-Yo Sell": start high to confirm exec sponsorship, get delegated down to directors/VPs for the work, then come back up to senior leaders to close (Ian Koniak — "Episode 8")
- Champion = "somebody able to get you in front of the right people" — work through champions to execs; only go around when they can't/won't get you to power (Ian Koniak — "Episode 8")
- Chris Stuart's Three C's: Committed (not merely interested) / Certainty (these activities lead to it) / Contribution (to whom?) (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Chris Stuart")
- RAD Goals: Reason (strong why) + Ambitious (out of comfort zone) + Drastic action (Ian Koniak — "My 2026 RAD Goals")
- "In order to do, you must first be" — write what you'll have done in 12 months, then ask "who must I become?" and journal the being (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Chris Stuart")
- **The Sound Bite (deal in two sentences, four blocks):** "Because of [change/shift], now is the time for [non-obvious response]; this lets you avoid [bad outcome] and unlock [good outcome]." Write one per top account, lay side by side — if they look the same, they're not sharp enough (Ian Koniak — "How to Win 7-Figure Deals…")
- **Numbers, Names, Dates** — the 3 things missing from most messaging. Numbers = size/severity/frequency of the problem; Names = the internal catchphrase/code name; Dates = timeframe on anything important (Ian Koniak — "How to Win 7-Figure Deals…")
- **Russian-nesting-doll structure:** the sound bite sits inside the executive summary, which sits inside the one-page business case — same core message expanding outward as the deal progresses (Ian Koniak — "How to Win 7-Figure Deals…")
- **3 messaging mistakes:** start late not early; sell *to* people not *with* them; focus on numbers not narrative ("people decide on the narrative, then justify with numbers") (Ian Koniak — "How to Win 7-Figure Deals…")
- **Recap = next steps only, never look backwards:** save discovery/fit reasons for the proposal stage; selling points in a recap dilute the action item (Ian Koniak — "Never Send Long Recap Emails…")
- **Be the Buyer, not the Seller:** frame discovery as YOU qualifying whether THEY fit ("Before I show you anything, I want to understand you to see if it's even aligned") (Ian Koniak — "The #1 Key to Winning Deals…")
- **Why Change / Why Now / Why Us**, anchored by **Cost of Delay** — what doing nothing costs per month in the metric they care about (e.g. agent attrition × revenue per agent = millions/month) (Ian Koniak — "Tale of the Sale: Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices")
- "Create the news, don't report the news" — reposition a passive ask (database/leaderboard) into an active solution that drives the outcome (Ian Koniak — "Tale of the Sale…")
- Write the requirements only you can meet: "When you write the requirements based on what only your company can do, competition ceases to exist." (Ian Koniak — "Tale of the Sale…")
- Hyper-personalization vs. relevancy: customization = specific to the person; relevancy = "I know what this persona in this sub-industry is going through." Both beat AI-spam openers (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with @Jake_Dunlap…")
- Singles & doubles to quota, triples & home runs to 300% — never put your whole year in one deal (Ian Koniak — "He closed a 75M deal at Oracle…")
- Add-Value-First formula: add value → then discovery → then pitch; deliver ~25 of 30 min as value before asking for the sale (Ian Koniak — "Sales 101: Add Value first")
- Discovery sequence: ask (1) problems + why they took the meeting, then (2) desired outcomes / "what does good look like," THEN prescribe; 2/3 of meeting on them, last 5 min on "here's where I can help" + book the next call (Ian Koniak — "1 Biggest Mistake you can make on a discovery call")
- Doctor's-prescription model: doctors ask what's wrong and dig deep before prescribing — never lead with your meds/credentials (Ian Koniak — "1 Biggest Mistake…")
- Activity → pipeline math: work backward from quota using close ratio ($500K at 50% = $1M pipeline = ~$100K/wk), then break to daily appointment targets (Ian Koniak — "Sales is a marathon, not a sprint")
- RGA (Revenue Generating Activity): only 4 RGAs — set appointments, do appointments, prep for appointments, follow up; everything else is a distraction to delegate/cut (Ian Koniak — "FEED YOUR FOCUS, STARVE YOUR DISTRACTIONS")
- 7-figure formula: right vehicle + right OTE (~$300K+) + attainable quota (~$2M) + few focused accounts (1-5, go high/wide/deep) + selling to the exec suite + mix of singles/doubles plus big hits (Ian Koniak — "Is it possible to make over 7 figures in sales")
- Get-motivated formula: find your WHY → write a measurable, stretch, accountable 12-week plan → execute daily ("12-Week Year") (Ian Koniak — "How to get motivated in sales!")
- Rest Generating Activity — "rest is the ultimate RGA": 4 vacations/yr booked 6 months out, 7+ hrs sleep, hard stop end-time (Parkinson's Law forces efficiency) (Ian Koniak — "How to Work Less - and Sell More")

### VOC language
- Internal seller pain: "I was my number… I was a terrible father… angry about not being able to hit this number which I identified myself with." (Ian Koniak — "He became a strategic seller with 4,000 accounts!")

- Emotional vs. flat framing: agents "losing grip" in the digital era (urgent/identity threat) vs. "agent productivity improvement" (not urgent) — same product (Ian Koniak — "Episode 3…")
- Trust signal: "I feel like we are his only account." (Ian Koniak — "Episode 3…")
- Stuck-rep pain: "I never had a formula." / "I just truly didn't want to do the work because I don't know how to do it." (Ian Koniak — "Episode 8")

- Underperformer self-talk: "I 100% attached my identity to my number." / "My standards were the bare minimum to get by." / "It felt harder than it needed to be." (Ian Koniak — "Matt Livingston Interview")
- Buyer's ROI justification: "At the very least I'd get my money back in commission, which has happened." (Ian Koniak — "Matt Livingston Interview")
- Desire a DFY/coaching offer speaks to: "I wanted somebody to put their arm around me and say: here's exactly what you do and everything's going to be okay." (Ian Koniak — "Matt Livingston Interview")
- Buyers buy on narrative, justify with numbers — "don't get caught up early in ROI figures; that just validates a decision already made." (Ian Koniak — "How to Win 7-Figure Deals…")
- Anything important to an exec gets an internal catchphrase/code name (e.g. IKEA's "the imagination gap") — find and echo their exact words (Ian Koniak — "How to Win 7-Figure Deals…")
- 2025 exec priorities to anchor to: "consolidation, resilience, optionality," OpEx/headcount reduction — "deliver more of an outcome with less people." (Ian Koniak — "How to Win 7-Figure Deals…")
- Why clients actually buy: "Because you stayed on top of me… you won't take no for an answer. This is something I really wanted to do." (Ian Koniak — "Sales Mastery Video Series 1: Follow up")
- Change-agent's fear: "If we don't change right now we'll go the way of Blackberry and Kodak." (Ian Koniak — "Tale of the Sale…")
- Disqualify language: prospects wanting "a quick fix," "one or two sessions," who show up "cross-armed" and "just want to learn more" are not buyers (Ian Koniak — "The #1 Key to Winning Deals…")
- Soft no / brush-off: "This doesn't necessarily align with how we're thinking about it… we'll let you know if something changes." (Ian Koniak — "1 Biggest Mistake…")
- After a value-first call: "I want more — whatever that was, I don't know what it was, but I want more." (Ian Koniak — "Sales 101: Add Value first")
- Buyer trust gate: "People don't want to share all their info until they know you're legit, credible, you have value to add." (Ian Koniak — "Sales 101: Add Value first")
- Pain language for sales-leadership offers: "Only 3 of my 12 reps hit plan." (Ian Koniak — "1 Biggest Mistake…")
- Overworked-seller pain: "You're working nights, working weekends… it feels like you're killing yourself and not getting the results you want." (Ian Koniak — "How to Work Less - and Sell More")
- Dream outcome: "When you're making seven figures you can go anywhere you want… afford a lifestyle of any proportion." (Ian Koniak — "Is it possible to make over 7 figures in sales")

### Offers / pricing / guarantees
- Incentives must carry a believable story, never a bare discount: "We're a public company finishing the quarter strong," "incentives for new logos this month" — the reason must be true (Ian Koniak — "How to Use Incentives without Being Pushy")
- Non-discount incentive menu that still creates urgency: a free month of service, 60-month pricing on a 36-month term, extra product at no charge (Ian Koniak — "How to Use Incentives without Being Pushy")
- Downturn entry offer: a free/complimentary business-value assessment — low-risk foot-in-the-door that becomes deep discovery and surfaces ROI (Ian Koniak — "It's about to get REALLY ugly in sales - get ready!")
- Reference existing footprint as warmth/risk-reversal: "You're already using us, you already have an MSA/PSA in place." (Ian Koniak — "How to Book Meetings with Senior Execs in 2025")
- Free-assessment / risk-reversal (Ricoh): "I'm offering a complimentary assessment of your total printing costs… and if we can't save you at least 20%, I won't even propose anything." (Ian Koniak — "The #1 Key to Winning Deals…")
- Same-price upgrade close: "For the same price we'll swap out all your equipment, pay off your existing leases, get you faster gear, and roll it into one managed fixed fee." (Ian Koniak — "The #1 Key to Winning Deals…")
- Free strategic engagement as trojan horse: Salesforce "Ignite" workshops given free "in exchange for considering our solutions"; prerequisite was 1:1 access to the entire C-suite (Ian Koniak — "Tale of the Sale…")
- High-ticket coaching ladder: "starts at $3,000, up to $48,000" — requires the buyer invest ≥1-2 hrs/week (a 1-2 year identity change) or "it's not the program for you" (Ian Koniak — "The #1 Key to Winning Deals…")
- Tiered offer ladder + low-risk CTA: "I have programs for every budget — online, group coaching, or one-on-one… book a free strategy call, we'll see if it's a fit, and if not it's all good either way." (Ian Koniak — "I spent $191,400 on personal development")
- ROI-justification for high-ticket: "$20K feels like a lot, but if it takes your income from $240K to $720K, the ROI is ridiculous." (Ian Koniak — "I spent $191,400 on personal development")
- Discovery → custom-plan two-call close: discovery is purely discovery; "Set up another time and I'll come back with a custom plan / prescription." (Ian Koniak — "1 Biggest Mistake…")
- Soft transition-to-close after value: "Sounds like there's a lot here we can help on… we won't get through it in 30 min. If you're interested in working with me, I'd love to continue." (Ian Koniak — "Sales 101: Add Value first")
- Coaching offer positioning (qualify by pain): "If you're working nights and weekends, killing yourself, not getting results — you're a good fit… we train you to be a top performer without sacrificing family/health." (Ian Koniak — "How to Work Less - and Sell More")

### Objection handling
- Pre-empt timing pressure (take-away close): "I don't want to show you the incentive if it's not feasible — is there any possibility you could do this this month?" ~9/10 say "show us what you've got." (Ian Koniak — "How to Use Incentives without Being Pushy")
- Cost-of-inaction reframe: ask "What happens if you do nothing at all? What does that mean to you?" then sit in silence — the buyer fills it with the cost of status quo (Ian Koniak — "He became a strategic seller with 4,000 accounts!")
- "Not interested" reframe: don't re-pitch the same value — change the frame to the buyer's biggest fear/identity threat and add urgency (Ian Koniak — "Episode 3…")
- Rebuilding a dead deal after a "no": low-ask value touches ("eight points of connection") — forward a relevant report with your comments, hand-deliver a printout, give without asking for the next meeting (Ian Koniak — "Episode 3…")
- Rebuttal to "keep cold emails short": "Whoever told you that hasn't sold a million a year in enterprise. You win by being specific about exactly how you help, not by being generic." (Ian Koniak — "How to Book Meetings with Senior Execs in 2025")
- Reframe "I have a bad hand": "Your contract's in place, they need these things, you're sitting on a multi-million-dollar expansion, not a bad hand." (Ian Koniak — "Episode 8")
- Reframe selling-to-execs as collaboration: "We're on the same side of the table, selling together to your board — they already want it. It feels like collaboration, not selling." (Ian Koniak — "Episode 8")
- Reframe call reluctance: "If we know at the other end there's contribution — because we've prepared, studied, trained — we're much more likely to pick up the phone." (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Chris Stuart")
- Cold-call reframe (the bar is low): "If you call and say 'I talked to X, Y and Z at your company, noticed these areas we can help with' — you sound different and people pick up because they don't get calls like that." (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Chris Stuart")
- Channel that beats voicemail: "Record an audio voice memo and send it via text — most will listen to that vs. a voicemail from an unknown person." (Ian Koniak — "Fireside Chat with Chris Stuart")
- Soft close that removes pressure: never lead with "it's expiring this fiscal." Ask first — "Before I propose anything: is signing in a three-week window even doable? If not, no worries at all." Then work backwards from go-live (Ian Koniak — "He closed a 75M deal at Oracle…")
- Disengaged-prospect reframe: "Help me understand — why'd you take the meeting? Sounds like everything's working well. Unless I'm missing something, help me out here." (Ian Koniak — "The #1 Key to Winning Deals…")
- AI-will-kill-software objection: reframe AI from a separate pitch to table stakes — "It's no longer complimentary, it's baseline. It should be baked in, not a bolt-on." (Ian Koniak — "He closed a 75M deal at Oracle…")
- "You're 3x too expensive" reframe: don't drop price — change the frame from the narrow ask to the bigger problem so price-comparable competitors no longer compete (Ian Koniak — "Tale of the Sale…")
- No-response ≠ rejection: "It's not rejection unless they said no. Stay on top of them — people will respect it and eventually say 'thank you for staying on top of me.'" (Ian Koniak — "Sales Mastery Video Series 1: Follow up")
- Lead-with-ego reframe: talking about your portal/platform/credentials "leaves customers completely disconnected" — you can't offer a solution until the customer says "here's where we need help" (Ian Koniak — "1 Biggest Mistake…")
- Problem → don't-jump-to-solution: most people jump to the fix; instead dig — "Why did they miss plan? Where do they struggle — discovery, prospecting, closing?" (Ian Koniak — "1 Biggest Mistake…")
- "Can't stop at 5pm" objection: "If you're working nights and weekends, you're working inefficiently — saying yes to people-pleasing, internal meetings, requests from people who aren't serious, and small deals." (Ian Koniak — "How to Work Less - and Sell More")
- Price-of-coaching reframe (Jim Rohn): "Work hard at your job, make a living; work hard on yourself, make a fortune" — find someone who's been where you want to go and pay them (Ian Koniak — "I spent $191,400 on personal development")

### Frameworks / formulas
- **Objection-handling sequence:** Understand → Empathize → Isolate → Address → Commit to action ("Help me understand what you mean" / "If budget wasn't an issue, would you still move forward?" / "So if I get that done, can we move forward?") (Ian Koniak — "Objection handling 101")
- **Elevator-pitch formula: "We help X do Y so they can Z"** — X=persona/vertical, Y=what you deliver, Z=business outcomes; tailor X, keep Z outcome-focused (Ian Koniak — "Perfecting your Elevator Pitch")
- **"Sell the grass, not the seed"** — describe the outcome delivered, not how the product works; "people don't buy the product, they buy the outcomes." Plus the "so simple your grandma understands it" clarity test (Ian Koniak — "Perfecting your Elevator Pitch")
- **POV / "Gap" narrative:** (1) state where they're trying to go (quote their CEO/COO); (2) show the obstacles you found (quotes at ground level); (3) pivot to how you fill the gap — "the big contrast between their vision and their reality." Dream→obstacle→bridge (Ian Koniak — "From Burned Out at 55 to Best in Company at 58")
- **"Interview, don't pitch"** — approach with intent to understand whether you can help, not to sell; a deliberately-imperfect POV works better because it invites correction ("It's actually better if it's wrong") (Ian Koniak — "From Burned Out at 55 to Best in Company at 58")
- **The 5 P's (teach-a-problem framework):** Problem, Primary reason, Pain, Promise, Payoff — used to educate a prospect about a problem they didn't know they had, before pitching (Ian Koniak — "4 Steps to become a Trusted Advisor")
- **4 Steps to Trusted Advisor:** (1) become an expert on the problem (customer stories, "drink your own champagne"); (2) teach via the 5 P's; (3) listen/assess/qualify the real pain; (4) show the full PLAN (solution + implementation/training + what the customer must provide), not just the product (Ian Koniak — "4 Steps to become a Trusted Advisor")
- **Pain vs. Gain:** people buy for one of two reasons — escape a pain/problem, or reach a gain/desired outcome they can't reach today; diagnose which before demoing (Ian Koniak — "Are we over complicating sales?")
- **Recession messaging (3 tips):** ignore the noise → focus on RGAs (revenue-generating activities) → adapt the message (reduce cost / do more with less / save time); lead with empathy; end on a "call to interest," not a call to action (Ian Koniak — "How to Sell More during a Recession")

### Offers / pricing / guarantees
- **Tiered coaching architecture:** Bronze = the portal ("everything I did to become the #1 rep at Salesforce" — hundreds of bite-sized 5–10 min videos + templates + workbooks); Silver = portal + weekly live group coaching + cohorts + private community; Gold = everything + 12 one-on-one sessions (annual payers can stack all 12) (Ian Koniak — "Is Ian's Sales Coaching Platform right for you" / "It's your fault you're missing your number!")
- **Scarcity/exclusivity stack:** one-year program capped at 100 members; live spot counter ("only 69 spots left"); hard close date ("closing May 16th"); reopen penalty ("once closed, I won't reopen for six months"); sells only to a waitlist ("1,400 on the waitlist, ~70–75 spots") (Ian Koniak — multiple)
- **Offer-as-gap-filler ladder:** "My program fills the gaps managers/companies aren't training." Three ways to help: teach you how (DIY) → do it with you (group/1:1) → do it together (Ian Koniak — "It's your fault you're missing your number!")
- **Future-Dated Order (FDO):** "Signature now, start date later." Locks the deal at current momentum, delays billing — "I don't need payment right now, just signature on the order form." Removes the cash-flow blocker without touching ACV (Ian Koniak — "How to address 'No Budget' objections")
- **Split payment / split invoice:** keep full ACV, change the billing cycle (annual→quarterly); "same pricing as if they paid in full" while splitting; delivery gated on payment ("first two sessions for half, pay the rest to schedule the last") (Ian Koniak — "How to address 'No Budget' objections")
- **Incentive ≠ discount:** reward larger commitment with volume pricing ("commit to all four workshops vs. one = a big price break"), not a price cut — preserves ACV (Ian Koniak — "How to address 'No Budget' objections")
- **Risk-free / no-pressure consult CTA:** "You've got nothing to lose. 45-minute call — if we can help, we'll share what that looks like; if we can't, we won't present anything. No hard closing, no pressure." (Ian Koniak — "The #1 Problem Keeping Sellers Stuck")
- **Risk-reversal cost assessment:** "If I can't help you or save you money, we won't propose. But most of the time we save 10–30% on your printing cost — would you be open to a discussion?" (Ian Koniak — "How to Sell More during a Recession")
