- Proprietary-mechanism + dream-metric headline: "Introducing: The Reply Method For Double Digit Replies" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Introducing: The Reply Method For Double Digit Replies")
- Referral subject line that nearly always gets opened: "Spoke with Nick" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 5 Data-Backed Cold Call Scripts to Overcome Any Objection")
- Pattern-interrupt re-open after a hang-up: "You and I last spoke on October 19th around 2:30, and admittedly, you hung up on me. I promise I did some prep for this one..." — specificity + light guilt (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 5 Data-Backed Cold Call Scripts to Overcome Any Objection")

### Frameworks / formulas
- **One-page business case (5 parts):** priority-driven headline → problem statement → recommended approach → target outcomes → required investment. Black font, white page, no branding so it "feels internal" to the exec, not vendor-y. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Build a One-Page Business Case…")
- **Priority-driven headline:** name the deal using the exec's own shorthand/codeword for what they already care about so you don't have to persuade — e.g. "Closing the imagination gap to drive digital order bundles." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Build a One-Page Business Case…")
- **Outcomes mirror the problem:** state target outcomes in the *same metric* used in the problem statement, shown as current → future by a specific date. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Build a One-Page Business Case…")
- **Reverse-engineer sales math:** desired commission → revenue → deals → pipeline coverage → intro calls → daily outbound activities. Benchmarks: ~30% win rate on qualified opps; 60–80 outbound activities per booked meeting. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Driving Accountability and Empowering Sales Teams…")
- **Income-goal math (consumer version):** want → cost (after-tax $) → $ per booked meeting → prospects-per-meeting ratio → prospects/month. Worked: $5,423/mo ÷ $168/meeting = 33 meetings × 27 prospects = 891 prospects/month. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How Many Cold Calls Does It Take To Afford a Baby?")
- **Permission + reason that benefits the prospect:** "Would it be okay if I asked you two or three direct questions? This way I can pinpoint our demo to what's most important to you versus generic things that waste your time." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Ask Tough Sales Questions…")
- **Teachable moment:** shift from "surface a problem → does it resonate?" to "show them how you solve it," led by a specific number tied to one value-add. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Open & Close More Deals…")
- **1-2-3 prospecting / buying-committee model:** 1 account, 2 departments, 3 contacts (and: 3 people, 2 departments, ≥1 with power to buy). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Build a Cold Calling Culture" / "The Perfect 5-Step B2B Sales Process (Mark Kosoglow)")
- **SDR job = sell the meeting, not the deal** (avoid AE-level discovery on a cold call). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Build a Cold Calling Culture")
- **Problem → Value** (timeless DR cold-email backbone): "People like you run into problems like this" (problem) + "people like you achieve these outcomes with our help" (social proof = value). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Write Cold Emails That Get Replies")
- **The Deeper Problem formula:** "The hard part isn't [surface thing], it's actually [deeper, more nuanced thing]" + value/outcome. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Write Cold Emails…")
- **The Want-But formula:** "[Persona] wants [aspiration], but runs into [challenge]" + social proof — works especially well on aspirational executives. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Write Cold Emails…")
- **Before-and-After formula:** problem + social proof naming a similar client + a one-line testimonial pulled straight from the case study (don't link the whole thing). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Write Cold Emails…")
- **ACE objection framework** (Accept → Consent → Explore): genuinely accept (don't "yes-but"); ask permission to ask a direct question; then explore with a close-ended, slightly cheeky question. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Roleplay With The World's Weirdest Sales Trainer")
- **The "coffee machine test":** phrase the prospect's problems exactly as they'd vent to a colleague at the coffee machine — their language, not product voice. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Roleplay…")
- **Four attention levers in outreach:** Volume, Offer, Relevance, Delivery — "Offer" (what they get from saying yes, unrelated to your product) is the most under-used and AI-proof. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Cold Email Strategy That Actually Books Meetings in 2025 | Jason Bay")
- **Three offer types (escalating power):** (1) Pitch the blind date — hype the AE/SE they'll meet; (2) One-to-many — a high-value benchmark/report; (3) One-to-one — a custom audit/analysis built for them. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Cold Email Strategy… | Jason Bay")
- **Triple-threat demo follow-up:** (1) group recap email + MAP; (2) separate 1:1 thread to each attendee asking personal feedback; (3) one-line "How do you think it went?" to the champion. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Close Deals FASTER… | Anthony Firenzi")
- **Three levels of exec presentation — Why / What / How:** lead execs with the Why (80% need only this), give the What as a 5-min "harbor tour" of hero features, save the How for technical buyers only. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Close Deals FASTER… | Anthony Firenzi")
- **5-stage buyer-centric sales process** (each = Stage + Seminal question + Exit criteria + Approvers + Gives/Gets): Initiate → Interest → Investigate → Validate → Justify → Decide. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Perfect 5-Step B2B Sales Process (Mark Kosoglow)")
- **Gives-and-Gets discipline:** every give (case study, demo, audit) is framed to extract a get — "are you deciding in a month or 6 months? That changes which case study I'd send." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Perfect 5-Step B2B Sales Process (Mark Kosoglow)")
- **Influence the required capabilities to be ordered** so your differentiators rank as the most important evaluation criteria. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Perfect 5-Step B2B Sales Process (Mark Kosoglow)")
- **Coach the 5 right calls, not 50 random ones; coach closed-lost, not in-flight deals** (reps are open about deals they've already let go). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Coaching Blockers Out of Sales Teams (Levi Thomas, CaptivateIQ)")
- **Problem Proposition (replaces value prop):** lead with the "hairy, meaty movie-scene problem" — persona + company + when it happens + painful-feeling word — then one sentence on how you solve. 90% problem / 10% solution. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Fixing the WORST Cold Call Pitches")
- **Two golden rules:** "You cannot be perceived to be better until you are first perceived to be different" and "your product's value only exists in the context of the problem that value solves." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Fixing the WORST Cold Call Pitches")
- **SNS test** — kill any line that "Sounds Nice but Signifies Nothing" (optimize, streamline, single source of truth, AI-powered); use "dumb human language" instead. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Fixing the WORST Cold Call Pitches")
- **Reverse Pitch:** pitch a problem a similar customer has + social proof, then ask "how does that compare to your experience?" — pull the buyer toward you instead of pushing. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Watch Me Tear Down 3 Real Cold Calls")
- **Mr. Miyagi objection method (3 steps):** (1) agree with / "play dead" on the objection, (2) incentivize conversation via a question, (3) sell the test drive, not the car. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 15 Best Sales Tips of 2024" / "Triple Your Cold Call Meetings" / "The Most Confusing Objection in Cold Calling")
- **Presupposition (Josh Braun):** "My guess is you've already looked into [X] before, huh?... and nothing could handle the complexity of your [situation], huh?" — removes pressure, gives an out. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 15 Best Sales Tips of 2024")
- **Cold email = Business Initiative × Industry Trend × Trigger/observation** (Kyle Coleman). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 15 Best Sales Tips of 2024")
- **Magic Moment question:** when a prospect agrees to a problem, turn it into a story — "When did you realize that was a problem? My guess is you didn't wake up yesterday and think this — when was the moment?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 15 Best Sales Tips of 2024")
- **1-through-10 demo/discovery close:** "10 is the best thing you've seen, 1 the worst — where are you?" then "what made it a 9?" (value) and "what would've made it a 10?" (the gap). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 15 Best Sales Tips of 2024" / "Get Ahead of Deal Killers")
- **Demo the Why (Rob Friedland):** bad outcome (status quo) → story of status quo → game-changing feature → story with product → good outcome. Say what it *means*, not what it *is*; one demo is ~15 mini-demos. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Demo Framework That Actually Closes Deals")
- **Popcorn Pricing (Belal Batrawy):** anchor with an inflated list price (small popcorn they'll never buy), make the premium tier only slightly more than the middle so it looks like a steal. Max 3 options, ideally 2 — more options lowers buyer IQ. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Present Pricing the RIGHT Way")
- **Floor + Range pricing:** "Our pricing starts at $18K — the floor — but typically for companies your size it's $34–56K. There's a couple factors. Before I go on, what's your initial reaction?" Surface price early to qualify budget + access to power. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Present Pricing the RIGHT Way")
- **Discounts vs. Upgrades:** discounts = hard savings; upgrades = things that cost you nothing but carry perceived value (free refill, admin seats, price-lock, waived implementation) — assign each a $ amount and show it "waived" in the premium tier. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Present Pricing the RIGHT Way")
- **Red/Yellow/Green light champion model:** with 8–10 buyers per deal, multi-threading's job is to turn red→yellow→green; one person can torpedo a deal. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Creating Champions Who Will Advocate for Your Deal")
- **Discovery Tree (3 layers):** Situation (how they do it today) → Operational problem (champion's daily annoyance = 4-5 figure pain) → Executive problem (C-suite risk = 6-7 figure pain). Climb to sell bigger deals. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Santa Unwraps 12 Sales Tactics")
- **5 agreements (sell in stages, not meetings):** Problem → Solution → Power → Commercial → Vendor approval. Ask "what am I trying to GET," not "what am I trying to do." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Santa Unwraps 12 Sales Tactics")
- **Four levers of transparent negotiation (Todd Caponi):** contract term, volume, timing of cash (prepay), predictability (sign-by date). Tell the buyer openly: "Which one are you willing to pull to bring your price lower?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Santa Unwraps 12 Sales Tactics")
- **PASS framework for cold email = Problem → Agitate → Solve:** notice the pain, show the factual cost of it, map to your value prop. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Break Into Enterprise Accounts With (Non-Cringey) AI Emails")
- **Triple-bypass to pass the gatekeeper (dose info only when asked):** 1) Slide-by ("could you get me over to [first name]?"), 2) lean on context/who-else-you-work-with, 3) lean harder on social proof; always end on a question to keep control. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Get Past The Gatekeeper")
- **PLAN next-steps acronym:** Pivot to the future, Logistics (who/when), Agenda (what + why), Next steps + expectations (mutual action plan). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Get Ahead of Deal Killers")
- **Match CTA to buyer-journey stage** (unaware→aware→consideration→evaluation): the less mature the buyer, the softer/value-giving the CTA; asking an unaware buyer for a meeting = "asking a stranger to marry you on the first date." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Break Into Enterprise Accounts With (Non-Cringey) AI Emails")
- **Pain Chain:** break one long problem "essay" into 8–10 short value-giving email touches that tell a connected narrative (problem → consequence → consequence), each teaching one lesson + offering one piece of content. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Stop Asking for Meetings in Cold Emails")
- **Awareness-laddering sequence:** run an "unaware pain chain"; track opens/clicks; when someone opens 3+ times or clicks, move unaware → aware → considering, then ask for the meeting. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Stop Asking for Meetings in Cold Emails")
- **The Reply Method:** (1) 1-to-1 look/feel without hours of research; (2) think in frameworks, not templates; (3) lead with a "world-class offer," not a demo ask. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Introducing: The Reply Method")
- **Email CTA rule:** don't ask for time or open-ended "are you having this problem?"; ask for interest ("interested in chatting further?") OR make a world-class offer (benchmark/analysis/audit). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Introducing: The Reply Method")
- **Banned cold-call openers:** never use "How's your day going?" or "Did I catch you at a bad time?" — both flag you as a telemarketer. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Triple Your Cold Call Meetings")
- **"Trap question":** pre-write ≥1 question per competitor that asks how the incumbent does the ONE thing only you can do, so the prospect discovers your differentiation themselves. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Triple Your Cold Call Meetings")
- **"Hairy lollipop specificity":** describe the prospect's problem with concrete sensory detail (e.g. "3,000 applications on day one of posting") so it evokes emotion; vague problems don't trigger. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Triple Your Cold Call Meetings" / "Unconventional Cold Call Approaches")

### VOC language
- Exec priority shorthand named in-house: "the imagination gap" — buyers coin codewords for what matters; mirror them. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Build a One-Page Business Case…")
- Early-stage price push, verbatim: "Can you just show me your product?" / "Just tell me the price." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Ask Tough Sales Questions…")
- "Lack of momentum kills all deals" (reframe of "time kills all deals") — diagnose with "Are we meeting regularly?" + "Are the meetings moving us forward?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Open & Close More Deals…")
- "The perfect talk track on the wrong prospect is still the wrong talk track." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Build a Cold Calling Culture")
- "Sales is a transference of feeling" (Zig Ziglar) — "you still want to buy from people you like and trust." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Build a Cold Calling Culture")
- They "reject you not because of interest but because of bandwidth." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Open & Close More Deals…")
- Generic/too-obvious problem language to AVOID: "A lot of VPs of sales are really focused on generating pipeline" (= "a lot of doctors are focused on making people healthy"). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Write Cold Emails…")
- Specific/triggering rewrite: "A lot of ops leaders want to remove production bottlenecks, but the shortage of welding talent makes that really tough right now." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Write Cold Emails…")
- Buyer fatigue stat as VOC: "58% of buyers report they waste the majority of their time in meetings with salespeople." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Cold Email Strategy… | Jason Bay")
- The dreaded stall, verbatim: "Before we even do that, I'm going to take this back to the team. We'll have a conversation and let you know what we think." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Close Deals FASTER… | Anthony Firenzi")
- Incumbent objection, verbatim: "We're already working with somebody else… we started ~18 months ago… it'd be too much disruption to rip something we just implemented." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Roleplay…")
- Busy-season brush-off, verbatim: "I appreciate the call, we just have so much going on right now… maybe reach back out when things aren't as crazy." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Roleplay…")
- Dream-outcome elicitation Q: "What would make it great — to the point you'd say there's no way I'd ever change, even if the impossible offer came along?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Roleplay…")
- Painful-feeling words that make prospects feel the pain: frustrated, anxious, concerned, "think it's ridiculous," annoyed. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Fixing the WORST Cold Call Pitches")
- Lawyer pain, verbatim: "the most mind-numbing part of their job is having to log their life in six-minute increments just to bill their clients" / "piece together a time sheet yourself at 10:00 on a Sunday." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Fixing the WORST Cold Call Pitches")
- CFO pain, verbatim: "immensely frustrating to waste hours at the end of every single month cleaning up the books"; "surprise expenses after a sales team offsite." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Fixing the WORST Cold Call Pitches")
- Insurance-defense firm pain: "fed up with all the deductions, rejections, and appeals they get on the e-bills they send to their carrier clients after they win a big case." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 15 Best Sales Tips of 2024")
- Buyer sticker-shock reactions worth anchoring against: "Wow, that's way more than I thought" / "That's what I thought it might be" / "That's a car's cost." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Present Pricing the RIGHT Way")
- Permission/secrecy phrase, now reusable: "between you, me, and the wall." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Creating Champions Who Will Advocate for Your Deal")
- Loss-aversion close-lost objections that signal you over-demoed: "This might be more software than we need," "We're just not there yet," "We're not ready for this." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Get Ahead of Deal Killers")
- Buyers arrive stating a WANT ("I want to get better at sales," "I need more leads") — the real NEED sits a layer beneath. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Get Ahead of Deal Killers")
- Gatekeeper instinct phrases reps trigger: "Whoa whoa, what's this regarding?" / "What company are you calling from?" — their job is to "detect and reject pitches." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Get Past The Gatekeeper")
- Email read as AI/spam = instant stop: buyers ignore anything that "sniffs as manipulative, sniffs as fake personalization, sniffs as AI" — em-dashes are a telltale AI sign to strip. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Break Into Enterprise Accounts With (Non-Cringey) AI Emails")
- The dismissive brush-off tone: "Fine. How can I help you?" (exasperated sigh) = "I know you're a telemarketer, just get on with it, I'm waiting to reject you." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Triple Your Cold Call Meetings")
- The "confused" objection: "Oh, we've already got a solution for that" — but their solution isn't what you do (e.g. "I've got a gym membership" vs. a SoulCycle class). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Most Confusing Objection in Cold Calling")
- Top-5 objections = 74% of all objections: "Not interested" (most common), product fit (17%), no budget, "I don't handle this" (not my responsibility), and getting hung up on (11%). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 5 Data-Backed Cold Call Scripts")
- Product-fit objection phrasing: "I heard it's not made for enterprise companies" / "you guys don't scale well with public companies" — often heard secondhand in a peer group. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 5 Data-Backed Cold Call Scripts")
- Buyer's reflex to any explanation: "Ah, this person's trying to pitch me" — and they're "already one foot out the door." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Most Confusing Objection in Cold Calling")

### Offers / pricing / guarantees
- **Price-is-dependent-on-value reframe:** "Price is based on a variety of criteria. We have clients that pay $10K, some $100K, some a million. I don't expect you to be in that large range — I had a few questions so we get the right footing on what range you could be in. Would you be okay with that?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Ask Tough Sales Questions…")
- **Required-investment honesty as a credibility lever:** don't minimize cost/effort — "We will not hit this outcome if you're not prepared to make this investment." Offer "a sliding scale of outcomes based on what you are or are not going to invest." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Build a One-Page Business Case…")
- **Free-audit-as-offer, concrete examples:** cybersecurity risk/posture benchmark vs competitors; website/cart/SEO audit; mystery-shop competitors' support response times; comp benchmarking — turn end-of-cycle proof into the upfront hook. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Cold Email Strategy… | Jason Bay")
- **Risk-reversal CTA for "send me an email":** "I'll send a 5-minute calendar invite for the same time tomorrow. If you don't like what you see, just decline the invite; if you do, keep the time." Never leave a cold call without a calendar next step. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Cold Email Strategy… | Jason Bay")
- **Pilot/trial give-to-get guardrails:** only run a pilot with (1) written success criteria and (2) a decision-maker who knows; set price expectation upfront ("if you like it, the last 5-10 min covers our programs, which start at $49,500"). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Cold Email Strategy… | Jason Bay")
- **The proposal/roadmap is a give, not a handout:** "Let's book a session — first half I'll walk you through new roadmap stuff (roadmap is 'crack for buyers'), second half we discuss the proposal." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Perfect 5-Step B2B Sales Process (Mark Kosoglow)")
- **Commercial carrot to manufacture urgency:** concession needn't cost money — billing terms, free month, extra seats, sign-by-date: "If you're a best-fit deal signing by [date], I can get my CRO to sign off on a better deal." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Close Deals FASTER… | Anthony Firenzi")
- **Lead-with-problem web copy that works:** "Legacy timekeeping solutions create a costly disaster — frustrated professionals, missed revenue, and zero insight… Revenue leakage: missed billable time, no operational insights, blind AI investment." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Fixing the WORST Cold Call Pitches")
- **Concrete tier architecture:** small = full list price, no discounts (anchor); medium = discount + small implementation reduction on 1-yr; large = bigger discount on 2-yr + waived implementation both years + free integration. Keep the A→B gap small so they leap up. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Present Pricing the RIGHT Way")
- **Quoting high can accelerate deals (bigger ≠ slower):** a high price forces power into the room earlier; small deals draw nitpicky below-the-line buyers and take longest. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Present Pricing the RIGHT Way")
- **Free perceived-value levers to stuff the premium tier:** price-lock vs 3–7% annual increase, waived implementation fee, dedicated implementation manager, usage buffer (e.g. 15% overage), advisory session, two-way integration reserved for the top plan. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Present Pricing the RIGHT Way")
- **Don't overshow product** → the buyer associates the premium price with bloated features they didn't want; "leave meat on the bone" (demo 2 of 3 problems, tease the third). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Get Ahead of Deal Killers")
- **Discount-for-commitment levers stated openly:** longer term, higher volume, prepay upfront, predictability — "we're willing to pay you in the form of a discount if you commit to signing by a certain date." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Santa Unwraps 12 Sales Tactics")
- **"World-class offer" beats a demo ask:** lead the CTA with tangible value (industry benchmark, custom analysis/audit, peer intel) so the buyer has a reason to meet even if they won't buy — +28% reply rate vs asking for time. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Introducing: The Reply Method")
- **Objection-handling offer architecture:** free lead magnet ("18 objection talk tracks, scripts written out") under a paid course with lifetime access, "dose it in 5 minutes a day," money-back guarantee, watch-this-video discount code. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Introducing: The Reply Method")
- **Risk-reversal close on a course:** "Remove the excuse. Give it a shot. If it doesn't work, we have a money-back guarantee. But I promise this will get you more meetings, make you more money, and help you make it to President's Club." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Introducing: The Reply Method")
- **Cold-email reply-rate data (use to justify copy choices):** buzzwords ≈ -57% reply rate; the word "AI" ≈ -⅓ reply rate; asking for time ≈ -44%; a world-class offer ≈ +28%. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Introducing: The Reply Method")
- **Sell the blind date, not the marriage (offer of value):** "Worst case, I'll look through your current plans and tell you if you're over-insured, so even if you don't move to us, I'll point out ways to cut costs." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Santa Unwraps 12 Sales Tactics")

### Objection handling
- **Third-strike concession (turns a no into a future yes):** on the 3rd objection, stop handling — "You're probably right, this wasn't a good time. I'll stay in touch via email — mind if I send a 5-minute invite in 30 days just to see if anything's changed?" (~⅓–½ say yes; most convert). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Build a Cold Calling Culture" / "How to Break Into Enterprise Accounts…")
- **Irrelevant question → acknowledge + ask permission to reframe:** "I appreciate the question. Can I give you context on how our current clients think about this, because it's a little different than how you're approaching it — would that be okay?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Ask Tough Sales Questions…")
- **Disagreeing without confrontation:** "I appreciate you sharing that. Would you be open to me sharing another perspective?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Ask Tough Sales Questions…")
- **Asking for power without "who's the decision maker":** anchor price range, name who you believe signs, then offer a low-pressure out: "When I give people the chance to just roast me without me pitching, they find it valuable… Do you think Sarah would like that, or is that a terrible idea?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Ask Tough Sales Questions…")
- **"Send me an email":** Accept, get consent, explore with humor — "Is that because your inbox doesn't have enough emails already?" / "Is this just a polite way to tell me to go away?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Roleplay…")
- **"I'm not interested" (fast = brush-off):** don't acknowledge, challenge with humor — "Is my voice that bad?" Distinguish brush-off vs real objection by SPEED of response. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Roleplay…")
- **"We already work with someone else":** "I'd be surprised if you weren't. Does that mean you've decided to never look at another supplier?" then "What would make it great?" to find the gap. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Roleplay…")
- **"You're too expensive":** "Appreciate that — when you say expensive, does that mean pricing is your #1 priority?" 90% say no (it's about value); price on a cold call usually means you talked too much about yourself. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Roleplay…")
- **"I need to take this back to the team":** blame yourself to disarm — "Am I going way too fast? Normally when I hear what you're describing it's a good fit and people move quickly. How about tomorrow instead of later today?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Close Deals FASTER… | Anthony Firenzi")
- **Reveal the buying process instead of hiding it:** "Normally the CPO wants to see the tool, the CFO wants the commercials to make sense, and the CEO wants alignment with company initiatives" — prescribing the path builds credibility and speed. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Close Deals FASTER… | Anthony Firenzi")
- **Prevention beats handling:** the less you say about yourself, the fewer things they can object to; "The pause" — answer every objection with a beat ("Hm, okay.") to listen, buy thinking time, and avoid the defensive "yes-but." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Roleplay…")
- **"Send me an email" (acknowledge emotion first):** "Sure, sounds like I caught you on a job site" — they're objecting to the interruption, not the offer. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Watch Me Tear Down 3 Real Cold Calls")
- **"No budget" (sell the test drive):** "Totally get it. My guess is you'll probably never buy this — but when budget frees up, the folks who get it know what's #1, 2, and 3 on the list. Open to a look, just in case?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 15 Best Sales Tips of 2024" / "The 5 Data-Backed Cold Call Scripts")
- **Negotiating-for-sport:** Chris Voss label, delivered slightly confused not accusatory — "It seems like you just want a good deal here." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 15 Best Sales Tips of 2024")
- **Late-cycle indecision (Jolt Effect):** stop discovering, start recommending — "We have this package, but I wouldn't do that one — I'd go here, it reduces complexity for you." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 15 Best Sales Tips of 2024")
- **Feature you don't have:** first ask intent ("If you're asking about analytics, what are you hoping to analyze?") — usually a different tool is failing; three routes: redirect, frame the gap as an intentional protective decision, or "on the roadmap." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Demo Framework That Actually Closes Deals")
- **Champion who won't sell upward:** "Between you, me, and the wall — I've seen VPs 9/10 times not care when they hear that. Can I give you a couple things that'll actually resonate with them?" — feed the champion the business case. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Creating Champions…")
- **Never say "perfect"** when a buyer shares a problem — signals "wolf ready to pounce." Respond with curiosity: "Oh really, how did that happen?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Present Pricing the RIGHT Way")

### Frameworks / formulas
- **PPO / Purpose-Plan-Outcome agenda (1 min):** Purpose (why we're here) → Plan (how we'll spend the time) → Outcome (the decision we'll make at the end). Each call's outcome seeds the next call's purpose+plan so agendas "talk to each other"; re-interject if rapport drifts. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Structure The Perfect Discovery Call" / "8 BRUTAL Discovery Lessons…")
- **The Five-Minute Drill (qualify/close fast):** three questions in order — (1) Do you want to buy? (2) When do you want to buy? (3) How do you buy? — and #3 is a statement, not a question ("This is how you buy"). Ask "must-have or nice-to-have?" BEFORE setting a next step; always suggest people + process, never "what should the next step be?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Structure The Perfect Discovery Call" / "8 BRUTAL Discovery Lessons…")
- **The 90-Second Rule (9-2 rule):** in the first 90 seconds prove you did business research on them (a launch, new office, webinar) instead of weather/sports small talk. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Structure The Perfect Discovery Call")
- **The Triple Bypass Method (gatekeepers):** dose info bit-by-bit only when pressed — (1) Slide By ("Could you get me over to Mike? It's Nick." no last name/company), (2) Context ("It's about the press release for the new Rochester office"), (3) Social Proof ("We work with a few other Buffalo firms… would you give him a heads up?"). Always end on a question to keep control. Demeanor = "act like you own the building": minimum info, slightly rushed; never lie, never pitch, never befriend. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Tactic Every SDR Needs for Gatekeepers")
- **The Mr. Miyagi Method (objection handling):** (1) agree with the objection to disarm, (2) incentivize them to share more via a "trap question," (3) sell the test drive, not the car / use what's "really going on" as the reason to act now. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How I Handle 'Call Me In 6 Months'" / "We Already Have A Vendor for that Objection")
- **30-60-90 future-pace close:** frame signing as the starting line; walk days 0-30 / 31-60 / 61-90 and the results to expect at each so the buyer feels they're partnering with you. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How EXPERT Sales Reps Handle 'NO'")
- **Buyer awareness ladder (Unaware → Aware → Consideration → Evaluation; aka AESS):** match message altitude to where the reader is — too-advanced loses the unaware; too-basic disqualifies the expert. - **The Pain Chain:** write one persuasive essay on the prospect's problem, then bust it into 5-8 emails, each teaching one linked problem that cascades into the next (no time to research → poor targeting → weak messaging → low engagement → blast volume → blacklisted). - **75/25 email ratio:** 75% about them/education, 25% about you. Structure: you have this problem → why it exists → things you could do → here's how we help. Concise is the #1 predictor of email success. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "What Great Sales Teams DO DIFFERENTLY")
- **The REPLY Method (5-part cold email):** Relevance (line 1 shows intent) → Problem ("why change?") → Value + social proof (name-drop similar company; +40% reply) → CTA (one, specific, closed). - **Freemium as long-game close:** push a price-mismatched prospect to the free product — "our freemium is so successful they usually come back." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Keep it Simple When Selling to Execs | Morgan Melo")
- **Rip-and-replace value stack:** at the demo, quantify time saved + value to team + cost AND the discount they'd get off the existing tool by dropping it, so the new tool nets cheaper. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "We Already Have A Vendor for that Objection")
- **Risk-reversal / no-show insurance:** get the calendar invite accepted live ("I'll send a placeholder now — mind hitting accept? Sometimes these land in spam") because Google hides invites from non-engaged senders. "Don't drop the baby." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 10 Brutal Cold Calling Lessons…")
- **Self-quantifying offer (perceptual curiosity):** assign the prospect homework to tally their own closed-lost "status quo" pipeline; they return with a bigger-than-expected number ($53M, $84M) and now THEY pull you in. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Start Discovery Calls with Instant Credibility")
- **Outbound > inbound economics (value claim):** cold-call-sourced leads cost ~25% of marketing leads AND convert better. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "This 4 Billion Dollar Company Uses AI to Supercharge Sales")

### Objection handling
- **"Call me in six months" (full sequence):** agree to remove pressure ("there's almost zero chance you'll buy in six months"), incentivize info ("just so no one else calls you in the next six months… what's going on?"), use what's going on as the reason to meet now ("avoid the whole dog-and-pony of demos — are you completely against a 15-min look next week?"). Take-away kicker: "Some people just want to tell me to go away — is that what's happening, or should I actually call in six months?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How I Handle 'Call Me In 6 Months'")
- **Ask a question instead of countering ("blast walls"):** buyers brace for you to rebut; seeking to understand first lowers the wall. Don't flinch — diagnose "brick wall vs something we can get around vs knowledge gap." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How EXPERT Sales Reps Handle 'NO'")
- **Gatekeeper won't budge:** stop after 1-2 shut-downs (Gong: a gatekeeper cuts cold-call success ~39%) — go around: mobile numbers, off-hours (CIO works later than their assistant), switch channels. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Cold Call Objection Tactic Every SDR Needs for Gatekeepers")
- **"Not now / six months out" in a deal:** back to discovery, then trade-off: "based on what you wanted to solve, it sounds like it might not be worth solving for the next six months, and it's okay if those things burn for now — am I hearing that right?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Structure The Perfect Discovery Call")
- **"They just want a demo":** redirect exit criteria — "Let's pretend the demo goes well… it's an investment of your time and mine. Could you actually see the team investing in this, based on the problems we discussed?" Then shut up. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Structure The Perfect Discovery Call")
- **Champion won't introduce power (yes-and):** "No problem. What conditions need to be true for you to feel comfortable involving those people?" Turns a fight into surfacing their real conditions. Single-thread test: "If Jamie left next week, who'd care about this and pick it up?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How EXPERT Sales Reps Handle 'NO'")
- **"We already have a vendor / competitor":** don't attack — agree first: "I totally get it, I should've assumed you had a tool, and 9 times out of 10 it doesn't make sense to switch." Then a trap question exposing a hole they discover themselves: "Just so no one from my team calls you again, you must not be doing any stock-option bonuses in your merit cycles, right?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "We Already Have A Vendor for that Objection")
- **Incentivize BEFORE you get curious:** don't dig right after a no — insert an incentive: "just so nobody on my team calls you again," "just so I know to mark this dead," "just so I can tell my manager you weren't a fit." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 10 Brutal Cold Calling Lessons…")
- **Empathize with status quo before challenging (Brent Adamson):** tell them they're right before you tell them they're wrong — "I can see why that's been beneficial…" then "one thing WE were surprised by collectively…" (same side of the table, never "I'm surprised YOU don't do this"). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Start Discovery Calls with Instant Credibility")
- **"Sell the test drive, not the car":** never close on a cold call — the only goal is one small step forward, then sell once they're in. Remove pressure: "My guess is you'll probably stay with [Competitor], but would you be open to a look — not for now, just so you know it's out there?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "We Already Have A Vendor for that Objection")
- **Yes/no answer + stop:** "Clarity and simplicity drive confidence." Answer "Yes, we can do that, a couple customers do it a couple ways" — then go silent. A 5-min monologue to a yes/no question reads as "can't do it." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "You Should Never Negotiate Over Email")
- **Bring up deal-killers first:** "Before our next call, can I share why prospects typically don't move forward — usually timing, priority, or budget. Do any feel like an obstacle?" Soft-close at every touch ("does Tuesday 1pm work?") to surface the real blocker. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "15 Expert B2B Sales Tips in 7-Minutes")
- **Earn the right to negotiate (price-too-expensive):** "Pretend we and everyone else cost the same — independent of price, are we your vendor of choice?" If no, you haven't earned the negotiation. Pre-frame timeline/price-creep with the CFO as bad guy; "get their number first" so every give earns a get. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Use This One Trick to Close Deals Faster")
- **Graceful price breakup (built-in bluff test):** "If your expectation was 15k, honestly we're probably not the solution — there are cost-effective products with reduced functionality; let me know if things change, I don't want to waste your time." Bluffers immediately surface hidden budget. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Keep it Simple When Selling to Execs | Morgan Melo")
- **Demo redirect (control without saying no):** "That's a cool part of our product, I'm excited to show you — but I want to stick to what we aligned on, and if there's time I'll show you that. Sound fair?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "#1 Sales Rep Runs The Exact Demo…")
- **Qualify-out / soft breakup:** "This doesn't feel like a priority for you right now" — they either agree (saves time) or start selling YOU on their interest. Too much eagerness makes buyers suspect a "Jedi mind trick"; cooling it flips the dynamic. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "30MPC Compilation: Discovery Call Tips")
- **Differentiate by teaching in discovery:** competitors ask the same questions — "teach your buyer something they don't know," aim for value even if they never buy. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "30MPC Compilation: Discovery Call Tips")
- **"Not my responsibility":** name the likely real owner; don't ask for a referral — get permission to name-drop: "Would you be completely against me mentioning we spoke?" then subject line "Spoke with Nick." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "LIVE COLD CALLS…")
- **Negative reverse / takeaway:** give them the out — "this is X, but he probably wouldn't be interested" — and if they lean in harder they'll usually help (e.g., give the referral). "Green Turkey": turn any answer into "that's exactly why I called." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "LIVE COLD CALLS…")
- **One "no" ≠ company "no":** "It's not companies that reject you, it's individual human beings" — go above/around a single brush-off. Tonality over words: "strong and wrong over weak and meek," 90% how you say it; train a "fake laugh" to disarm "not interested." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 10 Brutal Cold Calling Lessons…")
- **"It's easy to reject a salesperson; hard to reject a human being":** break the corporate-drone pattern with disarming bluntness so you become a person, not a pitch. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "This Cold Call Opener Has a 50% Success Rate")
- **Ghosted-deal re-engagement via reference:** instead of "any update?", "Customer X wants to connect with you — is your team still open to chatting?" A proactive reference is a non-generic reason to re-open. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Help Your Team Find & Leverage Warm Referrals")
- **Get-to-power CTA (name-drop, don't ask):** instead of "who else should we involve?", "Does it make sense to involve [Anna, your head of RevOps] next meeting?" — shows prep and removes their effort. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "6 PROVEN AI Sales Automations…")

### Hooks / headlines / subject lines
- Confession/relatable-lie open: tell a small embarrassing lie up top ("Don't worry, it was a lie" — told the ASPCA canvasser "I hate animals") to set up the real point. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Secret to Handling Nasty Cold Call Objections")

(30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Give a Compelling Pitch on Cold Calls")
- "Cold calling sucks — but that's why it works." Contrarian book-title hook that names the reader's resistance then flips it. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Give a Compelling Pitch on Cold Calls" / "The Ultimate Cold Calling Q&A")
- Re-trigger subject line from a personal detail only you two share: after a prospect rants about deep-dish, email subject "Pequod's > Domino's." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Sales Roleplay: How To Earn an Executive's Respect in 30 Minutes")
- Own-the-cold-call permission opener: "This is a cold call, but I promise it's well researched. Do you have a second for me to tell you why I called?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "I Taught A Standup Comedian To Cold Call (Real Dials)")
- Pattern-interrupt opener: "Hey [name], settle a little debate for me. Ribs the food, or ribs the body part? Winner gets 10 bucks." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "I Taught A Standup Comedian To Cold Call (Real Dials)")
- Self-deprecating gatekeeper hook: "It's Chip — like a potato chip or a chocolate chip, depends on if you're feeling sweet or salty today." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Working With Gatekeepers vs. Against Them (Chip Wooten, Motive)")
- Cold email line 1 = a fact about the prospect, zero pleasantries: "I saw the news regarding the new shipyard you opened in Portsmouth." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "12 Years of Enterprise Sales Learnings In 29 Minutes")
- Tiered, numbers-driven promise lead: "I'm going to show you the fastest way to close a $3,000 deal, a $30,000 deal, and a $300,000 deal." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "$3k vs $30k vs $300k Sales Close (Live Breakdown!)")
- Big-number proof + bold-guarantee headline: "We Analyzed 85 MILLION Cold Emails: This is How You GUARANTEE Replies." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "We Analyzed 85 MILLION Cold Emails…")
- Negation hook: "Forget Perfect Sales Calls — Here's the Only Outcome That Matters." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Forget Perfect Sales Calls…")
- Best cold-email subject lines name a physical action the prospect just took, boring + specific + ≤5 words: "Phase 2 pancreatic cancer study," "27 new employees," "curriculum map rollout." One-word lowercase "welders" pulled 90%+ opens. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "We Analyzed 85 MILLION Cold Emails…")
- Loss-aversion lead: "Big group demos are where most B2B deals go to die." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Software Demo Secrets That Instantly Close Deals")
- Identification lead that twists into the pain: "If you're anything like me, nobody ever really taught you how to sell… nobody ever taught you what to SAY to get the deal closed." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Product Roadmap: Q1 2025")
- Vivid pattern-interrupt: "Most Monday morning meetings put your sales team to sleep — and I'm here to throw your melatonin in the trash." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Running Sales Teams Meetings That Don't Suck")
- Reframe hooks worth swiping: "The difference between the top rep and the average rep isn't how hard they work — it's how they spend their time." / "The purpose of your vision isn't that you achieve it — it's who it causes you to be today." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How ELITE Sales Reps Structure Their Day" / "Steal Alex Kremer's 1-Minute Routine")

### Frameworks / formulas
- **Problem Proposition (vs value prop):** (1) describe a triggering problem in such specific detail it surfaces a painful visual memory, (2) one-sentence solution, (3) interest-based CTA. Gong on 300M+ calls: buzzword value-prop = 5.5% success vs problem-prop ≈16% (3x). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Give a Compelling Pitch on Cold Calls")
- **4 specificity layers** that make a problem "triggering": persona + annoyances + scenery/setting + emotion. ("Most CFOs of insurance defense law firms think it's ridiculous they deal with so many deductions, rejections, and appeals right after winning a big case.") (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Give a Compelling Pitch on Cold Calls")
- **Match the problem to the buyer's altitude:** same product, different pain per persona (billing manager = daily clicks; CFO = receivables/cash; attorney = no cash for acquisitions). Pitch the pain that persona actually feels, in their jargon ("compa ratio," "buried in a mountain of spreadsheets") not sales language. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Give a Compelling Pitch on Cold Calls")
- **Mr. Miyagi method (objections):** don't fight emotion with logic — (1) agree with the objection to remove sales pressure, (2) incentivize them to share more ("just so nobody from my team calls you again…"), (3) reintroduce logic/problem-prop to re-open. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Secret to Handling Nasty Cold Call Objections")
- **The 3 offers / 3 CTA levels that get a yes:** Easy = "blind date" (hype the expert they'll meet, not the product); Medium = one-to-many (a repurposable benchmark / state-of-industry report); Hard = one-to-one custom audit built in advance (reserved for dream accounts; best when it fuels your own discovery). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The 3 Sales Offers Elite Reps Use" / "We Analyzed 85 MILLION Cold Emails…")
- **Executive discovery sequence (7 steps):** open with credibility ("here's what I learned about you, what did I get wrong?") → anchor to a strategic objective → problem hypothesis → name the status quo → empathize with it → introduce an enemy to the status quo via a respected peer ("here's what Penn State didn't realize…") → high-impact close. Throughout: "seek to be corrected, not correct." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Sales Roleplay: How To Earn an Executive's Respect in 30 Minutes")
- **The 3 Whys (compelling reason):** Why do anything / Why you / Why now — and "why now" must carry a real date. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Make Your Sales Team Industry Experts | Todd Caponi" / "Effective Ways to Push Your Reps on Deal Risks…")
- **Make customers smarter about THEIR business, not yours** — lead with industry expertise (headwinds/tailwinds, how the buyer is measured); most reps are "given a nail and told to find a hole." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Make Your Sales Team Industry Experts | Todd Caponi")
- **Tailored Permission Opener** = Trigger (about them) → own that it's a cold call → ask permission. Adapt only the trigger per persona; never change the framework. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Ultimate Cold Calling Q&A")
- **Triple Bypass (gatekeeper):** slide-by ("Could you get me over to Armand? It's Nick.") → return to context ("It's about that office opening in Tacoma…") → lean on social proof, not product ("We work with a couple other insurance defense firms in Buffalo."). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Ultimate Cold Calling Q&A")
- **Cold email structure (all about them):** Line 1 = observed fact/trigger tied to an objective; Line 2 = unsure tonality linking it to a likely problem; point to another customer (not yourself as hero); close with an easy yes/no CTA; personalization at the END as a P.S., never as bait up top. Audit for the "we/wee problem" (I/we/our/us). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "12 Years of Enterprise Sales Learnings In 29 Minutes")
- **Discovery via "seeking correction":** give the prospect a specific statement to react to, because correcting is low-effort: "It seemed like the business was focused on this objective… what did I get wrong?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "12 Years of Enterprise Sales Learnings In 29 Minutes")
- **Two closing questions (kill happy ears):** "Does this feel like a problem worth solving?" then separately "Is it worth solving right now?" — then shut up. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "12 Years of Enterprise Sales Learnings" / "Sales Roleplay…")
- **The Reply Method (cold email, <75 words):** boring 5-word subject → Reason (proves it's for them alone) → Problem (agitate current state, no ROI claims) → Value + Social Proof (a peer logo + outcome) → offer-based CTA → name. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "We Analyzed 85 MILLION Cold Emails…")
- **Five Agreements to close:** Problem → Solution → Power → Commercial → Vendor; stack into one call for hot SMB, spread across many for enterprise. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "$3k vs $30k vs $300k Sales Close…")
- **Invert the feature-benefit to find the problem:** flip "Streamline hiring with the fastest, most accurate background checks" to "slow down hiring with the slowest, most inaccurate checks" to surface what you actually solve. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "I Ran a Sales Call For A Product I Never Sold")
- **3-layer discovery tree:** Situation → Operational problem (5-figure, "pain in the butt") → Executive problem (6-figure: risk/cost/revenue); bridge from operational to executive with an emotional, painful story. Decision-drivers: "Does it make me money, save me money, or prevent me from getting sued?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "I Ran a Sales Call For A Product I Never Sold")
- **"Typically / multiple-choice" steer:** "When people have frustrations here it's usually one of three things — A, B, or C. Which is it for you?" (build options collectively exhaustive). Pair with **push-pull**: throw out a number then immediately hand them the right to deny it ("this probably costs ~$45k… or is this pennies in the barrel?"). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "I Ran a Sales Call For A Product I Never Sold")
- **Personalization layering beats customization:** "law firms" → "PI firms" → "PI firms in Reno" → "PI firms in Reno, 50+ attorneys, just acquired another firm" — one company-level point reused across every contact at the account. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "We Analyzed 85 MILLION Cold Emails…")
- **The "W" / exit-criteria frame:** before every call define the single win ("what will we high-five about?"); for discovery the only W = "found one problem we can solve + they agreed to keep exploring." Demo runs **headline → tell → show → confirm** ("I just showed you this — does it solve your problem, yes or no?" before moving on). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Forget Perfect Sales Calls…")
- **People buy emotionally, then justify logically** — lead with the emotional problem, save ROI/numbers for the justification phase. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "We Analyzed 85 MILLION Cold Emails…")
- **Above-the-line (priority-based) vs below-the-line (problem-based) discovery:** execs have already chosen 3–4 priorities; anything outside them is a waste of time. Problem/feature selling caps you at 4–5-figure deals; attaching to a funded board-level priority unlocks 6–7-figure deals. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Make $1M W-2 Closing Enterprise Deals" / "How to Train Sales Teams on Discovery… Eleanor Dorfman")
- **"How do they make money?"** as the master research prompt — relevancy cuts through; VPs/CEOs take meetings "to get smarter," not for use-cases. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The AI Playbook for Sales | Jake Dunlap")
- **5 Whys coaching:** ask "why" up to 5 times to hit root cause; phrase collaboratively ("why do you think the prospect feels that way?"), and how/what reads less aggressive than why. Model the skill live before coaching. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The '5 Whys' That Will TRANSFORM The Way You Coach Your Sales Reps")
- **Purpose-Agenda-Outcome (PAO) opener:** your expectations + their expectations + a clear mutually-agreed outcome, delivered as a back-and-forth, with a different outcome per call type (inbound vs enterprise intro vs close). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How I Kickoff Every Sales Call" / "Why Most Salespeople Fail at Discovery Calls")

### VOC language
- Kneejerk dismissive objections (rejecting the interruption, not the product): "I'm not interested." / "Call me in 6 months." / "Can you send me an email?" / "Whatever you're selling, I ain't buying." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Secret to Handling Nasty Cold Call Objections")
- No-budget in the buyer's words: "Right now there's just no budget for this type of thing." / "Budgets were released ~9 months ago and our cycle isn't coming for another 3–6 months — we have to go through this whole long approval process with our CFO." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How I Handle 'No Budget'")
- Price objection VOC: "RocketReach is too expensive, I've looked before" — distinguish "sticker shock of going $500→$10K" vs "didn't see enough value." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Nail Your Cold Calls… Lylle Ryals, RocketReach")
- Buyers skip 5-star reviews and read the 4s, 3s, 2s, 1s first — so case studies that "sound like five-star reviews" get ignored. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Make Your Sales Team Industry Experts | Todd Caponi")
- What execs actually want to hear: "What are you doing that I'm not? What do you know that I don't?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Sales Roleplay…" / "12 Years of Enterprise Sales Learnings")
- Competitor-squeeze line: "They do pretty much everything that you do and they're half the cost. So what can you do for me?" Hard anchor: "This is absolutely the most I can ever pay — no more than $100,000." Sticker shock: "That is the combination of every other tool in our HR tech stack combined times two." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "8 Real Sales Negotiations…")
- Timing-stall decoded: "We're just really busy right now" / "Call me in 3–6 months" usually = "I'm too nice to tell you no." And "I'm too busy" = too busy to rip-and-replace software, not too busy for a 15-min look. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Ultimate Cold Calling Q&A")
- Gatekeeper deflections: "We're really not interested" / "We've already got a system in place" / "We just signed a contract." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Working With Gatekeepers vs. Against Them")
- End-user dream-outcome reframe: the person "on call 24/7" where "if the website goes down it becomes their problem" → sold as time saved + risk removed. Stat: "82% of B2B decision makers feel sellers are completely unprepared for their first conversation." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Unlocking Buyer Pain Points… Maddy Jackson" / "12 Years…")
- Problem-surfacing prompts that pull real pain language: "What's the O in your OKRs?" / "What's keeping you up at night?" / "What's on your whiteboard right now?" / "What's red on your dashboard right now?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Forget Perfect Sales Calls…")
- "Sell them on what they're already sold on" (their priorities, their #1 blocker) — don't try to shift a buyer's priorities in cold outreach. Stat: 58% of buyers feel a sales meeting "wasn't worth their time." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "We Analyzed 85 MILLION Cold Emails…")
- Magic-moment question: "My guess is you didn't wake up yesterday and decide this was a problem — when did you actually realize it? Was something missed?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "I Ran a Sales Call For A Product I Never Sold")
- Buyer discount phrasings: "How can we sharpen the pencil?" / "We have other software providers that give us an 80% discount." Dodge before the ask: "I've got to talk to my team internally / let me get back to you." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Key Steps to Make an Immediate Impact…" / "Why Most Salespeople Fail at Discovery Calls")
- Construction-buyer pains (specific/swipeable): "losing 10–20% of extra work-order tickets," "not getting paid on change orders," "paperwork emailed around and lost in translation," "labor productivity." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Why Most Salespeople Fail at Discovery Calls")

### Offers / pricing / guarantees
- **Offer-based CTAs beat asking for time** (Gong data): asking for a meeting drops replies ~44%, open-ended/problem CTAs −29%, interest-based +7%, but offer-based (give value for time) +28%. Examples: "Interested in benchmarking [Company A] against [competitor]?" / "We ran a benchmark with a few of your peers — want to see how you stack up?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "We Analyzed 85 MILLION Cold Emails…")
- **Sell the meeting, not the product (no-budget):** "You don't want to be the person who loses budget when it opens up — let's pre-build your case so when budget frees up your ticket's already in line." Risk reversal: "Would you be completely against a 15-minute look — not for now, just so you know your options?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How I Handle 'No Budget'")
- **Bundle/value reframe vs a 10x-pricier product (Carta):** "A lot of CFOs are surprised they get all their accounting services free with us — that usually makes up for the $10K," then de-risk: "we can skinny it down or beef it up." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Nail Your Cold Calls… Lylle Ryals")
- **Pressure-removal close (opt-in + opt-out):** "Is this a problem worth exploring?" then "Is it worth exploring right now?" then a low-commitment next step with explicit permission to bail ("if you don't like what you see, tell me to cut bait"). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Sales Roleplay…")
- **Demonstrate-the-pain demo:** make the buyer run their current broken process first (e.g. a comp review across 3 spreadsheets), reveal the mistakes, then show the solution. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Make Your Sales Team Industry Experts | Todd Caponi")
- **Anchor high, then invite a counter** — "There's no cost to anchoring high"; pair with "we can skinny this down or scale it up — what did you have in mind?" so you never negotiate against yourself (9/10 come back higher than a pre-discount). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "8 Real Sales Negotiations…")
- **Discount discipline:** never discount without a timeline in return ("discount if you close before end of month," reinforce the expiry every call); when asked to cut price, **trade down** — "What do you want to take out to get there?" Concede only what costs you least (waive implementation, quarterly payments) and frame it as hard-won. Socialize any discount to every stakeholder. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "8 Real Sales Negotiations…")
- **One-cut discount play:** "I think I can get $300 off — but I need you to sign by Friday." Pre-draft the contract, delay sending ~1 hour so it looks like you fought finance. Force the close: "Is this the last discount you'll have to give — and how do you know that?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "$3k vs $30k vs $300k…" / "Effective Ways to Push Your Reps on Deal Risks…")
- **Manufacture a compelling event from cost-of-inaction:** a strong business case lets you create an "artificial compelling event" — "every month you don't adopt this, it's costing labor, lost revenue, missed retention" — better than discounting to quarter-end. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Effective Ways to Push Your Reps on Deal Risks…")
- **The Discount Menu (give-get architecture):** a fixed list of stackable levers the buyer pulls to earn a lower price — annual upfront, net-30, sign before trial ends ≈7.5%, three reference calls ≈5%, case study + logo rights ≈2% — with a hard ceiling. Removes negotiation awkwardness, raises ACV, accelerates cycles. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Key Steps to Make an Immediate Impact When Taking Over a Sales Team")
- **Offer value on the booked meeting even if they don't buy** (most sales calls they've sat through were bad). Voicemail roughly doubles cold-email reply rate; voicemail + cold call ≈ triples it. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Ultimate Cold Calling Q&A" / "8 Real Sales Negotiations…")
- **Risk-reversal program framing:** flip the ratio — "20% of time teaching, 80% reinforcing so it sticks" vs typical trainings that are "glorified YouTube videos with 15% completion rates." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Product Roadmap: Q1 2025")

### Objection handling
- **"I'm not interested":** "Shoot, this one's on me — you'd have reached out if you were interested. Just so nobody from my team calls you again, be brutally honest: solution already in place, not thinking about this at all, or you just hate cold calls? Totally fine if it's that third one." ### Frameworks / formulas
- **4-line signal/cold-email framework:** (1) reason for reaching out / observation off a trigger, (2) a problem you think they have, (3) social proof + value (similar company, outcomes), (4) short CTA. - **"Don't sell the signal":** never make the trigger the reason for outreach ("you opened my email 5x"); tie a fresh, separate trigger to your solution's value. Taco-stand rule: don't tell a hungry person they're hungry — show the sizzle. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Use Intent-Based Selling")
- **Problem Proposition (3 parts):** (1) triggering problem with "hairy lollipop" specificity, (2) one-sentence solution as an afterthought, (3) low-friction interest CTA — spend ~80% on the problem. **Hairy Lollipop Test:** the problem must be so dangerously specific the reader can SEE it. - **Triggering-problem layering:** base problem + persona + specific annoyances + time/place trigger + emotion ("they think it's *ridiculous* they have to deal with this"). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Flip The Cold Call Script: How to 'Reverse Pitch'")
- **Chunk up by seniority / above-the-line vs below-the-line (Skip Miller):** managers and below get the operational/process problem; Director/VP/C-suite get the business problem + outcome attached. - **Mr. Miyagi objection method (3 steps):** (1) laugh + agree to disarm (hit the emotional gut first — amygdala's firing, they're not listening to logic), (2) incentivize them to share ("just so no one calls you again, is it A, B, or C?"), (3) sell the test drive, not the car. - **Solution-agreement isolation test:** "If this were free, could you see this being something you'd want to use?" — separates fit from price. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Ultimate 5 Sales Stages | Nick & Armand")

### Objection handling
- **Disarm before logic / acknowledgment not apology:** never logically rebut a dismissive objection — agree and humanize first, but without lowering your status; never say "sorry." Match an absurd objection with absurd bluntness: "Where'd you get my number?" → "Totally my bad, it's from a provider called Banana Leads — want a screenshot of what they have so you can get it removed?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "42.5 Minutes of Cold Call Objection Handling")
- **"Not interested" reply (book the meeting, don't email):** "Thanks for letting me know — is my timing terrible, or is this just a bad fit?" Timing is workable; fit reveals the competitor. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "20+ Cold Email Templates" / "42.5 Minutes of Cold Call Objection Handling")
- **"No budget" agree-then-multiple-choice:** "It's hard enough to keep a tool right now, let alone buy a new one — you're practically bringing food stamps to your CFO. Just so no one calls you again: is budget completely out, or does anything you spend get run through 17 ROI cases?" then sell the 15-min look. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "I Handle EVERY Cold Call Objection" / "42.5 Minutes of Cold Call Objection Handling")
- **Sell the test drive, not the car:** "Honestly you're probably not buying this for 6 months — crazy idea, would you be completely against taking a look, not for now, just so you know it's out there when budget opens?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "I Handle EVERY Cold Call Objection" / "The Top 15 Sales Tactics of ALL TIME")
- **"Send me an email":** "Totally — can I ask one question so what I send isn't totally irrelevant?" then re-pitch the problem. An emailed follow-up books ~1 in 100, so book on the call; once they reply, CALL (the call now has relevance). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "42.5 Minutes of Cold Call Objection Handling" / "8 Brutal Cold Email TRUTHS")
- **"Not my responsibility":** restate the problem area to test if it's actually theirs; if truly someone else's, don't ask for a referral email — ask "Would you be completely against me mentioning that we spoke?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "42.5 Minutes of Cold Call Objection Handling")
- **They hung up:** don't redial pretending you got disconnected. Wait a week: "We spoke July 17th around 1:45 — you said you were slammed prepping for a meeting and admittedly hung up on me…" (light guilt + not-a-spam-dial). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "42.5 Minutes of Cold Call Objection Handling")
- **Preemptive strike + clarify-don't-counter on price (John Barrows):** "We're not the cheapest — nor do we want to be." To "you're too expensive" → "Compared to what? My competitors, missing quota this quarter, or losing your top reps? And do you mean total cost of ownership or the number on the proposal?" The first objection is rarely the real one. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Own the Sales Cycle")
- **Walk away on purpose / disqualify to build trust:** "Based on what you've seen — architecture, product, pricing — is there anything that could disqualify us from a next step?" then sit in the pause. If their top criteria are genuinely your weaknesses: "Those aren't my strengths; if that's truly what you're after, I'd point you to XYZ." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How To Avoid Competitors Undercutting Your Deals" / "Own the Sales Cycle")
- **Silence as the discount response:** nod, say "okay," stay quiet — buyers often re-justify or walk back ("…but we can always work on price"). For savvy procurement, break silence with the bundle-all-asks question. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Set Yourself Up for Negotiation Success")
- **"Same job" empathy reframe vs. procurement:** "I get that you have to sell this internally — I'm in the exact same spot, so I need to understand everything you need so I can go sell it to my team once." Stops repeated nibbling. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Set Yourself Up for Negotiation Success")
- **Surface objections early, on purpose (Dan Flood):** end a demo with "We could spend hours here — where do you see this working, and what are you skeptical about?" Unsurfaced objections brew into ghosting. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How To Win Complete Control of Your Deals")
- **Always give a reason for a hard question (John Barrows):** "I was wondering who else you're talking to — reason I ask is, if it's X/Y/Z it's apples-to-apples, but if it's A/B this gets hard to decide." Preempt "why do you need to know that?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Own the Sales Cycle")
- **The "I don't know" hold:** asked to hold a price next month, never say yes (deal slips) or no (looks desperate) — "I don't know, let's talk about it October 1st." Truthful uncertainty draws the buyer to create certainty and close faster. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Negotiation Masterclass" / "The 7 Deadly Sales Negotiation Sins")
- **Add the risk "half-lever" (Todd Caponi):** when legal piles on liability/insurance terms — "My pricing also assumes a reasonable amount of collaborative risk. What you're asking adds significant cost and risk, so the pricing model would have to change." Usually they just drop it. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Negotiation Masterclass")
- **Discount root-cause reframe:** buyers ask for discounts because of a price-value mismatch — fix the value articulation (right people, right pains) instead of pre-discounting. The 5-minute exec squeeze: "What's the one thing you need from me in these five minutes to earn the right to a longer conversation?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Real Reason Reps Miss Quota" / "Own the Sales Cycle")
- **Validate the problem before assuming pain:** audit the data first (law firms thought billing was bad until the audit showed they beat industry average — a non-problem). If a reframe doesn't land ("no, it's just slow"), eject — it's a bad-fit deal. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Ultimate 5 Sales Stages | Nick & Armand" / "The One-Page Business Case | Nate Nasralla")

### Frameworks / formulas
- **The 3x3 Cold Email:** (1) what you know about them + the problem it causes, (2) one-sentence solution, (3) low-friction CTA — no email longer than three short bodies. Problem → value → ask, tailored at the top. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Triple Your Email Replies With The 3x3 Cold Email")
- **Low-friction CTA language:** never "book a meeting / meet with a specialist"; use "open to taking a look?", "care to learn more?", "open to taking a peek?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Triple Your Email Replies With The 3x3 Cold Email" / "How to Close 90% of Leads… (Vin Matano)")
- **Problem Proposition (cold-call pitch):** ~80% of time on the problem, ~one sentence on the solution. Three parts: triggering problem → one-sentence solution → interest-based CTA. "If you nail the problem, the solution becomes obvious." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How Top Sales Pros Pitch to Win Every Time")
- **Triggering-problem sharpeners:** layer persona + annoyances + scenery (time/place it hits) + emotion. "CFOs say billing takes time" → "CFOs of insurance defense law firms find it ridiculous that deductions, rejections and appeals make billing take forever after winning a big case." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How Top Sales Pros Pitch to Win Every Time")
- **The Hairy Lollipop Test:** the problem must be so dangerously specific the prospect can literally *see* it ("the hair on the lollipop"). If they can't picture it, it's not specific enough. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How Top Sales Pros Pitch to Win Every Time")
- **One-sentence solution formula:** "We do [key differentiator] which allows us to solve [the problem we just described]" — then re-anchor back to the problem. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How Top Sales Pros Pitch to Win Every Time")
- **Chunk up for seniority:** below-the-line = process problem; above-the-line (VP/C-suite) = attach a *business* problem to it. "Buried under spreadsheets with 17,000 VLOOKUPs" (manager) → "…which makes it hard to ensure managers make equitable comp decisions" (CHRO). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How Top Sales Pros Pitch to Win Every Time")
- **Problem Tree (4 layers):** Situation → Operational problem (champion's complaint) → Executive problem (bad news a VP delivers to a CEO) → Business impact (C-level metric / board priority). Build by starting at the operational problem and "so-what"-ing down. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Teach Discovery Without Confusing the Hell Out of Your Sales Team")
- **Invert feature→benefit to find the problem:** flip a website benefit ("spend less time planning comp in spreadsheets") into the problem ("wasting time planning comp in spreadsheets"). (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Teach Discovery…")
- **Keenan's PICK chart:** Problem → Impact → Root Cause. A problem (low win rates) is NOT the business impact — the impact is the money/quota damage it causes; technical issues are root causes, not the business problem. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Fancy Discovery Questions Don't Work (Ask These Qs Instead) | Keenan")
- **Want → Why conversion:** when a prospect states a want ("get off spreadsheets"), convert to a why: "My guess is you didn't wake up yesterday thinking today's a good day to get off spreadsheets — what prompted wanting to switch?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Secret to Uncovering True Buyer Motivation… (Garrett Palmer, Pipedrive)")
- **Demo "P-pattern":** how do you do this? → here's how you can do it instead → how does this compare? Repeat 3-4x to keep the demo as continued discovery; structure the demo in the exact order of the pains they gave you. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Secret to Uncovering True Buyer Motivation… (Garrett Palmer, Pipedrive)")
- **KPIC demo framework:** "Here's what I Know" → the Problem → the Impact → Connect to how we solve it → CTA. "If you're not going to use what you learned in discovery, don't even do it." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The #1 Mistake Reps Make When Moving from Disco to Demo | Kevin 'KD' Dorsey")
- **BLC (Benefit-Laden Check) + make them hold it:** instead of "Does that make sense?", ask "How much faster is that than what you're doing now?" so the benefit comes out in THEIR words; then "What campaign would you start with? Who'd you roll this out to?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The #1 Mistake Reps Make When Moving from Disco to Demo | Kevin 'KD' Dorsey")
- **3-slide demo deck:** Slide 1 "What we heard" (3 bullets = problem + impact each); Slide 2 "How we solve each"; Slide 3 blank with their faces = "your demo wish list." Demo in before/after stories, never features. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "5 Terrifying Sales Ghosts That Will Haunt Your Quota | Halloween Special")
- **The 5-Minute Drill (end of every call), 3 questions:** "Do you want to buy?" (worth solving) → "When do you want to buy?" (directional go-live + contract dates) → "How do you buy." (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Most Important Steps of a Sales Call for Better Results")
- **Voicemail Double-Tap:** only ever leave two. VM1 = context only (~15s); VM2 = context + social proof (~30s). Point them to the email subject line; don't ask for a callback. - **4-part cold email structure:** (1) observation/research trigger, (2) problem + its impact, (3) solution matched to that problem, (4) interest-based CTA ("are you interested to learn more?" beats asking for a time — per Gong). - **Problem Prompter email + One Idea Rule:** one idea, one objective, one problem per email (so you can write emails 2/3/4 from the same research). ~68 words, lots of white space; ~9 seconds reading time = ~37 words. - **FIRE account prioritization:** Fit, Intent, Relationship, Engagement — tier 1-4, pour effort into 4-check accounts. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Close 90% of Leads… (Vin Matano)")

- **7 ways to get prospects talking:** be interested not interesting; hand them the mic; answer a question with a question; "the playback" (summarize, they yes-and you); trade cleverness for bewilderment; "Can you tell me more about that?"; force a 3-beat pause before responding. - **Giulio's 3-step objection framework:** 1) properly agree/accept, 2) ask permission to challenge ("do you mind if I ask a direct question?"), 3) ask a question to make THEM change their mind — never argue. - **One-cut negotiation (6 steps):** before — know BATNA/range, state price then shut up, gaslight/push away on the balk. - **Four Levers of Negotiating:** every price is built on (1) volume committed, (2) timing of cash / how fast they pay, (3) length of commitment, (4) timing of the deal. - **The "Fortunately" reframe:** never "unfortunately we can't" — say "fortunately we don't, because…" grounded in their numbers. - **POC pre-plan (mutual success plan):** key business outcomes → must-have vs nice-to-have ("what features, if missing, would prevent you from buying?") → milestones → handshake defining the bare minimum for "success → we move forward." - **Stage-based (not meeting-based) deal progression:** deals move only when exit criteria met; focus on what you need to GET (problem/solution/power agreement), not what to DO. Combine stages, never skip. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "The Sales Process Elite Reps Use (And You Don't)")
- **Shadow-based discovery:** ask to watch the painful manual process end-to-end ("a shadow says a million words") to "drag them through the glass and see where the blood is really being drawn." - **The 5 Tones (Jeremy Miner):** familiar-tone open (repeat name twice, stutter/pause, shuffle papers — triggers curiosity not fight-or-flight); use no-oriented questions ("Would you be against…?") over manipulative "yes" questions. - **Two-option architecture that wins either way:** 1-year at 150k vs 2-year at 250k that ramps 110k→140k — guarantees expansion + retention while saving them money year-over-year. (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How To Reframe Objections As Strengths David Rosenstein")
